title.rendered: Conquer Cancer fuels five groundbreaking studies

content.rendered:
Spring 2025
By Stephanie Lowitt
Photography by Sam Ogden

Conquer Cancer®, the ASCO Foundation, is on a mission to accelerate breakthroughs in lifesaving research and empower people everywhere to conquer cancer.  The foundation recently awarded a total of $550,000 to five Dana-Farber physicians pursuing novel treatment approaches.

Approximately 80% of gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GISTs), a rare cancer that forms in the wall of the intestinal tract, are driven by mutations in a specific gene. Tyrosine kinase inhibitor drugs (TKIs) can inhibit tumor growth, but patients can experience resistance to approved single-agent TKIs, and combinations of those TKIs are toxic. Candace Haddox, MD, is researching targeted therapies including a novel TKI combination, to assess its effect on GISTs and on patients’ quality of life.

Praful Ravi, MB, BChir, MRCP, is conducting the first-ever trial evaluating a new therapy for metastatic, castrate-resistant prostate cancer, an incurable disease with an average survival of 1-3 years. He is exploring a combination of targeted radioactive materials and carboplatin, a radiosensitizer that makes tumor cells easier to kill, while working to minimize damage to healthy tissue.

While over 80% of pediatric cancer patients become long-term survivors, they later experience cardiovascular mortality 7 times higher than the general population; and survivors of color experience twice that rate in large part due to social inequities like food insecurity. To refine a “food is medicine” intervention, Rahela Aziz-Bose, MD, is working to establish one of the first health equity interventions addressing disparities in longer-term pediatric cardiovascular health, an essential step toward survivorship equity.

Rosemarie Mastropolo, MD, is exploring how to improve the therapeutic patient-clinician relationship for adolescent and young adult (AYA) cancer patients, who experience challenges that are different from those of younger or older patients due to the varying degrees of patient independence and involvement of the caregiver in their treatment. This study will help define and measure the ideal patient-caregiver-clinician relationship for AYAs.  

Erica Pimenta, MD, PhD, is studying how insulin-like growth factor 1, a hormone that helps with growth, metabolism, and other bodily functions, may improve outcomes for patients with liposarcoma, a rare, malignant cancer that develops in fat cells and is the second most common soft tissue sarcoma.

excerpt.rendered: Conquer Cancer®, the ASCO Foundation, is accelerating discovery Institute-wide, from pediatrics to rare sarcomas.

jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The V Foundation is taking aim at acute myeloid leukemia in children with a grant that will enhance Dana-Farber's search for more effective and durable treatments.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Rally Foundation supports bold pediatric cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Rally Foundation for Childhood Cancer Research recently awarded $450,000 in grants to four Dana-Farber researchers developing innovative treatments for pediatric cancer.

title.rendered: Sajni Fund raises vital funds for rare pediatric cancer research

content.rendered:
Spring 2025
By Casey Repasy

At 7 and a half years old, Sajni Chakrabarti was diagnosed with a rare and aggressive brain cancer, diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma (DIPG), which affects about 300 children annually and currently has no cure. Nineteen months later, Sajni passed away—10 months beyond her initial prognosis—largely due to her bravery and courage in undergoing experimental treatments.

One of these treatments was the first personalized immunotherapy for DIPG at Dana-Farber, led by Susan Chi, MD, clinical director of pediatric neuro-oncology, and Mariella Filbin, MD, PhD, research co-director of the Pediatric Neuro-Oncology Program. While the treatment did not prove successful for Sajni, variations of it are now advancing through clinical trials, with Sajni’s experience serving as a catalyst for this critical research.

Since her passing, Sajni’s parents, Prabal Chakrabarti and Vanessa Ruget, have raised more than $300,000 to support Filbin’s pediatric brain cancer research. They have also directed donations to the arts program in Dana-Farber’s Jimmy Fund Clinic, which brought countless smiles to Sajni and her family during her treatment.

Sajni’s father reflects on the importance of funding childhood cancer research, saying, “Children’s cancer is a smaller market for drug development, and only receives a tiny fraction of federal grants. To address childhood brain tumors, it’s vital to give these flexible funds to efforts like the Sajni Fund, to light a flare a company can then follow with promise,” adding, “This is about saving kids’ lives.”

content.rendered:
Spring 2025
By Lori Dougherty
Photography by John Deputy, Sasha Pedro, and Samantha Yanofsky/SLY Photography

The Friends of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute hosted a variety of events throughout 2024 that raised more than $600,000 for lifesaving cancer research and patient care.

They kicked off the year with Friends Cure Cabin Fever in February at PKL Boston, where more than 100 guests joined the Friends for fun, philanthropy, food, and pickleball.

Evening with Friends in May attracted 150 guests for a discussion of how Dana-Farber’s dedication to discoveries in cancer research impacts our delivery of compassionate, patient-centered care, as well as an elegant dinner and live auction at the venerated Ritz-Carlton, Boston.

And at September’s In the Bag Luncheon, Friends enjoyed a curated silent auction of vintage designer handbags and a thoughtful program focused on the latest in cancer research at Dana-Farber, the increase in different types of cancer diagnoses among younger patients, and prevention and early detection of cancer.

Founded in 1976, the Friends of Dana-Farber have raised more than $59 million to fund powerful cancer research and patient care programs at the Institute. Their mission is twofold: raising funds, and providing services that enhance Dana-Farber’s healing environment, including gift bags for patients undergoing treatment, administration of our world-class art collection, non-denominational spiritual health programs, and programs to brighten the holidays for patients and families.

jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A Chance for Kids & Families raised $462,102 in 2025 for cancer research and patient care at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. Throughout the summer, patrons who donated to the Jimmy Fund at participating Burger King®, The Paper Store®, Uncharted, and Valvoline Instant Oil ChangeSM locations received a coupon, with all proceeds…

jetpack-related-posts.title: An Evening with Friends
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On May 4, the Friends of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute gathered for a special evening that raised more than $400,000. Since 1976, the Friends have raised more than $50 million for Dana-Farber’s lifesaving mission.

img.alt_text: A group of people in front of a Friends of Dana-Farber sign

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Chance for Kids & Families
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A Chance for Kids & Families raised over $425,000 in 2024 for cancer research and patient care at Dana-Farber. Patrons who donate to the Jimmy Fund at participating Burger King, The Paper Store, and Valvoline Instant Oil Change locations receive coupons, with all proceeds supporting Dana-Farber’s lifesaving mission.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Friends of Dana-Farber Annual Gala
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Friends of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute recently held their Annual Gala, raising more than $465,000. Evening with Friends featured cocktails, dinner, and a live auction. The Friends exemplify the “power of friends” through their dual mission: raising funds to support research, patient services, breast and gynecologic cancer programs, and oncology…

img.alt_text: Attendees of the Friends of Dana-Farber Annual Gala pose for a photo

jetpack-related-posts.title: Estate of Carolyn Brophy
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Estate of Carolyn Brophy has generously bequeathed $120,697.36 to support cancer research and care at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. Carolyn’s commitment to Dana-Farber’s mission will drive promising research and innovative treatments. Her legacy will inspire breakthroughs and improve patient experiences, helping Dana-Farber continue to defy cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Golf tournament celebrates $1 million raised
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: DefinitiveCares Charity Golf Tournament recently reached an incredible $1 million in total fundraising since its inaugural tournament in 2016. All proceeds go directly to Dana-Farber in support of lifesaving research and patient care.

title.rendered: Van Allen named to Chandra Nohria Family Chair for AI in Cancer Research

content.rendered:
Spring 2025
By Lori Dougherty
Photography by Justin Knight

Eliezer Van Allen, MD, was honored as the first incumbent of the Chandra Nohria Family Chair for AI in Cancer Research at Dana-Farber, at a celebration in November 2024. Endowed with a gift from Institute Trustee and Vice Chair of The Dana-Farber Campaign Monica Chandra and her husband, Nitin Nohria, this is the first chair in the field of artificial intelligence (AI) established at the Institute.

As Chief of the Division of Population Sciences, Van Allen develops algorithms to dissect high-dimensional data directly from cancer patients and uses these insights to address major open questions in the field. Van Allen’s research in computational biology and machine learning is helping to shape how AI can be applied to cancer medicine and research, including prevention and early detection, and has established the field of clinical computational oncology to advance precision cancer medicine worldwide.

excerpt.rendered: This endowed chair is the first in the field of artificial intelligence to be established at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute.

content.rendered:
Spring 2025
By Lori Dougherty
Photography by Pan-Mass Challenge

In September 2024, more than 400 cyclists took to the backroads of the Berkshires in Western Massachusetts and New York to experience PMC Unpaved, a gravel bike-a-thon that raises funds for Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. Riders chose fully supported routes of 30 or 50 miles beginning and ending at Camp Mah-Kee-Nac in Lenox, Mass., and enjoyed a full weekend of camp activities. A vital “spoke in the wheel” of the Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC), which is presented by the Red Sox Foundation and M&T Bank, PMC Unpaved riders contributed $1.2 million to the organization’s record-breaking gift of $75 million in 2024 and to its astounding cumulative total of over $1 billion raised since 1980. The PMC contributes 100% of every rider-raised dollar to Dana-Farber and is the Institute’s largest donor, accounting for 66% of the Jimmy Fund’s annual revenue. PMC Unpaved comes back for its fourth year in 2025, with the ride being held on October 4, along with a full weekend of activities.

excerpt.rendered: PMC Unpaved riders contributed $1.2 million to the Pan-Mass Challenge’s record-breaking gift of $75 million in 2024.

jetpack-related-posts.title: PMC Unpaved
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: PMC Unpaved is a gravel bike ride over the scenic backroads of the Berkshires in western Massachusetts that raises funds for Dana-Farber Cancer Institute.

img.alt_text: A group of bicycle riders riding along a wooded path

jetpack-related-posts.title: PMC Check Presentation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC) community came together at Rochambeau Restaurant in Boston on Sunday, Nov. 2, for the 2025 PMC Check Presentation.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Pan-Mass Challenge raises record $72 million to bring cures closer by the mile
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On long journeys, landmarks and milestones show us where we are and how far we’ve come. Since 1980, the Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC), the beloved bike-a-thon and the nation’s most successful athletic fundraiser, has seen plenty of both.

img.alt_text: Pan-Mass Challenge riders along the route

jetpack-related-posts.title: One in a billion: Pan-Mass Challenge surpasses $1 billion fundraising milestone
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In 2024, the Pan-Mass Challenge had a banner year, as the organization generated a record gift of $75 million and surpassed an extraordinary $1.047 billion in lifetime fundraising since its founding in 1980.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Pan-Mass Challenge celebrates PMC Pedal Partners from the Jimmy Fund Clinic at Fenway Park
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On May 17, dozens of PMC Pedal Partners—pediatric patients from the Jimmy Fund Clinic at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute paired with PMC riders and teams—gathered at The 521 Overlook at Fenway Park to meet the cyclists participating in the 46th PMC on Aug. 2 and 3.

img.alt_text: A family of four at Fenway Park

jetpack-related-posts.title: Pan-Mass Challenge makes record-breaking $78 million gift to drive Dana-Farber’s progress against cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC), a bike-a-thon that raises more money for charity than any other single athletic fundraising event in the world, has built an unparalleled track record for success strengthened by touchstone traditions and continuous improvements in pursuit of the goal of defying cancer.

img.alt_text: A child holding a 'We love PMC riders' sign among a group of bike riders

content.rendered:
Spring 2025
By Kayla McMahon
Photography by Dordick Trial College

The Dordick Trial College, led by renowned personal injury trial attorney Gary A. Dordick, raised an impressive $325,000 during its fourth annual event in Los Cabos, Mexico. This achievement brings the total funds raised to over $1 million, supporting the work of Steven Treon, MD, PhD, in Dana-Farber’s Bing Center for Waldenström’s Macroglobulinemia Research. The event offers trial lawyers and law firms a unique opportunity to network with and learn from industry leaders while coming together to combat this rare disease. Dordick’s dedication to Dana-Farber’s mission underscores the event’s significant impact on both legal education and cancer research.

excerpt.rendered: The event offers trial lawyers and law firms a unique opportunity to network and learn from industry leaders while helping to combat Waldenström’s macroglobulinemia.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dordick Trial College
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dordick Trial College, an annual legal education event held in May 2025 and organized by attorney Gary Dordick, raised more than $140,000 for Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s Bing Center for Waldenström’s Macroglobulinemia. The multiday program convened legal professionals for workshops and networking, with proceeds benefiting critical research and care for patients…

img.alt_text: Gary Dordick holding a large check for Dana-Farber

jetpack-related-posts.title: Lustgarten Foundation invests $1.5 million to bring promising immunotherapy to patients with pancreatic cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: When the Lustgarten Foundation was founded in 1998, fewer than 10 principal investigators across the U.S. had a primary focus on pancreatic cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Prevention is goal of groundbreaking immunotherapy trial
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: When asked what motivates her to support cancer research, Susan Hertog starts at the beginning, when her best friend was diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer at the age of 49.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Swim Across America
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Swim Across America’s Boston Open Water Swim raised $335,000 in 2025 to benefit patients who receive care at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and their families. Raising over $3.8 million since 1996, the organization continues to “Make Waves to Fight Cancer” and fuel critical survivorship research at Dana-Farber. This year's event will…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Fred and Michele Brettschneider
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Fred and Michele Brettschneider made a commitment of $250,000 to support a clinical trial network for Waldenström’s macroglobulinemia and advance all clinical research for this rare form of blood cancer within the Bing Center for Waldenström’s Macroglobulinemia.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Novel clinical trial in pancreatic cancer bolstered by $1 million gift
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: John Byrnes is a self-proclaimed “satisfied customer.” Diagnosed with stage IV pancreatic cancer in 2015, John is grateful for each and every day his Dana-Farber care team has given him.

content.rendered:
Spring 2025
By Lori Dougherty
Photography by John Deputy

The 2024 Presidential Symposium in September was a fitting send-off for Laure H. Glimcher, MD, who stepped down as president and CEO of the Institute on October 1. The event explored a strategic priority of Glimcher’s tenure and a central focus since the Institute’s founding, “A Patient-First Approach to the Future of Cancer Care.” Supporters of The Dana-Farber Campaign met incoming President and CEO Benjamin L. Ebert, MD, PhD, and heard updates from Institute leaders on areas of great promise for patients, including next-generation therapies, cancer care equity, and Dana-Farber’s proposed future cancer hospital. Presidential historian and Pulitzer Prize-winning author Doris Kearns Goodwin shared her own experience of Dana-Farber’s patient-first approach when her late husband, Richard “Dick” N. Goodwin, was diagnosed with cancer in 2017. She was joined by Dick’s oncologist, Glenn Hanna, MD.

excerpt.rendered: Event attendees explored Dana-Farber’s patient-first approach to cancer care with Institute leaders and special guest Doris Kearns Goodwin.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute Presidential Symposium
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In October, Dana-Farber supporters and leaders gathered for the annual Dana-Farber Cancer Institute Presidential Symposium. Attendees received firsthand updates on the State of the Institute, advances and opportunities in prevention and early detection, the impact of philanthropy on advancing research, and Dana-Farber’s world-renowned hematology/oncology fellowship program. Pictured are fellowship program…

jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: “Sparking Discoveries Through the Power of Community” was the theme for the annual Dana-Farber Cancer Institute Presidential Symposium in October 2023

jetpack-related-posts.title: Lubin Family Foundation Scholar Award Annual Symposium
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute celebrated its commitment to nurturing future leaders in academic medicine at the Lubin Family Foundation Scholar Award Annual Symposium, held on May 15, 2025.

img.alt_text: William G. Kaelin Jr., MD speaking at a podium

jetpack-related-posts.title: Phyllis and Richard Krock
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Institute Trustee Phyllis Krock and her husband, Richard, gave a generous gift of $100,000 to the Palm Beach Initiative. The funds are dedicated to the Presidential Initiatives Fund under Dana-Farber President and CEO Benjamin L. Ebert, MD, PhD. With this support, Dana-Farber physicians and researchers can continue developing innovative cancer…

jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Friends of Dana-Farber hosted a variety of events throughout 2024 that raised more than $600,000 for lifesaving cancer research and patient care.

title.rendered: The Dana-Farber Campaign: Closing the equity gap in cancer care

content.rendered:
Spring 2025
By Kathy Clute
Photography by Josh Campbell, Sam Ogden

A cancer diagnosis often brings fear, anxiety, and very real worries about how to pay for care or manage weeks or months of treatment. These concerns can be particularly acute for people in under-resourced or medically underserved communities, as they have higher rates of disease and often experience barriers to accessing and receiving care.

Funds from The Dana-Farber Campaign expand access, allowing us to reach even more patients and families by bringing high-quality treatments to underserved populations of all races or ethnicities, hastening the pace and reach of our clinical trials, and working to address disparities in cancer prevention, care, outcomes, and survivorship.

One example is the community-facing patient navigators who provide hands-on support to newly diagnosed patients who may need assistance overcoming obstacles to treatment for blood, breast, gastrointestinal, thoracic, gynecologic, and genitourinary cancers. Insurance does not pay for these services—the program is entirely funded by The Dana-Farber Campaign.

“I’m there to help with anything: transportation, food, anything that would hinder them from coming to their appointments and being successful in treatment,” said Judy Thyme, MSPH, the patient navigator for the Lowe Center for Thoracic Oncology. Since 2021, Thyme and her colleagues across six different types of cancer have helped nearly 600 patients via more than 4,000 touchpoints.

The Patient Navigation Program is just one initiative of the Institute’s Cancer Care Equity Program, established in 2012. Campaign funding subsidizes on-site clinics at two Boston community health centers, community cancer screenings, education and trust building programs, and research that includes more than 90 active clinical research studies and pilot programs aimed at uncovering and eliminating disparities in cancer care.

EQUITY IN ACTION

Adolescent and Young Adult Neuro-Oncology

Dana-Farber created this program and its multidisciplinary clinic in 2020 to bring highly specialized care to adolescents and young adult patients (ages 15-39) with brain tumors or other malignancies of the central nervous system.

Neuro-inclusive care

Adult patients with intellectual and/or developmental disabilities can benefit from the Institute’s new Neuro-Inclusive Care and Empowerment Program, launched in 2024.

Young-Onset Colorectal Cancer Center

The Young-Onset Colorectal Cancer Center, established in 2019, is one of the first of its kind to focus on understanding and treating the growing incidence of colorectal cancer in people diagnosed before age 50.

Tackling inequities in pediatric cancer

Even if they receive high-quality treatment, children with cancer from low-income households are more likely to experience a relapse or to die than their peers in higher-income families.

In a bold step to address this stark disparity, Dana-Farber is a founding member of IGNITE, a research consortium of pediatric oncology experts from 12 leading institutions nationwide. Established in 2024, it will focus on testing and scaling interventions that target social drivers of health such as poverty, food insecurity, housing instability, and lack of transportation.

“Instead of testing new drugs, we’ll be testing supportive care interventions that can change the landscape of pediatric cancer care for the better,” said pediatric oncologist Kira Bona, MD, MPH.

African DNA yields prostate cancer clues

It’s well-known that men of African descent have the world’s highest incidence of prostate cancer. But most of the studies documenting the genetic underpinnings of the disease have focused on individuals of European ancestry.

To remedy that, Dana-Farber researcher Timothy Rebbeck, PhD, co-led a study that analyzed the DNA of nearly 7,500 men in East, West, and South Africa—more than half of whom had the disease. They identified 15 risk factors in the men’s genomes, four of which had not been previously linked to prostate cancer. Their findings, published in Nature Genetics in 2024, help explain the elevated prostate cancer rates across the African diaspora and show why studying diverse populations is so important.

“Going forward, our work can be used to develop better risk assessment models for African American men and guide them to proper screening and treatment,” Rebbeck said.

jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Event attendees explored Dana-Farber's patient-first approach to cancer care with Institute leaders and special guest Doris Kearns Goodwin.

img.alt_text: Glenn Hanna, MD (left), and Doris Kearns Goodwin

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Your generosity has funded paradigm-shifting initiatives that lessen the burden of cancer for patients and families here and around the globe.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign: A future of possibilities
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: More people will need advanced cancer care than ever before, and the best place to deliver that care is in a setting solely dedicated to treating people with cancer.

img.alt_text: A medical professional embraces a patient

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Society
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Dana-Farber Society (DFS) is a group of visionary donors who are changing lives and creating a legacy through a planned gift such as a bequest, life income gift, or beneficiary designation to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, the Jimmy Fund, the Friends of Dana-Farber, or the Pan-Mass Challenge.

jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact

jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White

TA's flexible commitment plays a crucial role in driving progress and improving outcomes for patients and families.

title.rendered: The Dana-Farber Campaign: Stopping cancer before it starts

content.rendered:
Spring 2025
By Kathy Clute
Photography by Sam Ogden

If you have a higher-than-normal risk of being diagnosed with a cancer, wouldn’t it be ideal to be monitored and treated by experts before the disease has a chance to develop or progress?

That is now possible, thanks to The Dana-Farber Campaign. Building on advances in genomics and data science, the Institute in 2023 established the nation’s first integrated clinical and research program devoted to detecting and intervening in conditions known to be precursors for cancer.

The new Centers for Early Detection and Interception (CEDI) represents a fundamental shift toward proactive cancer care. Most cancers are diagnosed when a person already has symptoms—often when the disease has already advanced and is harder to treat or cure. But CEDI’s clinicians and scientists are laser-focused on developing and deploying new technologies and methods for detecting the disease earlier and on discovering innovative ways to intercept cancer before it fully develops or progresses.

“People at higher risk for cancer—whether because of genetic conditions, family history, or a previous cancer—can come to CEDI and learn more about their risk as well as possible treatment options,” said Irene Ghobrial, MD, director of CEDI’s Center for Early Detection and Interception of Blood Cancers and the Lavine Family Chair for Preventative Cancer Therapies at Dana-Farber. “These may include lifestyle modifications, immunotherapy, and personalized precision medicine to stop the cancer before it’s symptomatic.”

BRCA center pioneers prevention and treatment

Dana-Farber’s Mellen and Eisenson Family Center for BRCA and Related Genes is one of the few places in the world dedicated to preventing, researching, and caring for BRCA-related cancers. People with mutations in the DNA repair genes known as BRCA1 and BRCA2 have a significantly higher risk of contracting various cancers, particularly those of the breast, ovaries, pancreas, and prostate.

A priority for the center is developing tests for ovarian and pancreatic cancers, which are often only detected at an advanced stage because of a lack of effective screening measures. Dipanjan Chowdhury, PhD, center co-director and the Svanberg Family Chair at Dana-Farber, has developed a technology that can interpret microRNA patterns in blood to predict whether an individual has or will develop ovarian cancer. It is being tested now with the goal of winning FDA approval for clinical use.

Using AI to detect pancreatic cancer

Pancreatic cancer is typically discovered at a late stage, but innovations in genetic testing and artificial intelligence (AI) are making it possible to catch the cancer earlier before it has a chance to spread. At the Hale Family Center for Pancreatic Cancer Research, researchers are leveraging AI to:

• Develop a risk assessment tool that can comb through millions of electronic medical records to identify patients with symptoms that could be predictive of pancreatic cancer.

• Create an algorithm to identify very early pancreatic cancers on CT scans and other imaging tests.

• Apply novel deep learning techniques to large, single-cell genomic datasets to understand how pancreatic cancer cells change their identity to evade treatment.

Rapid blood test could save lives

Dana-Farber researchers have invented a rapid CRISPR-based molecular test that could enable more patients with two forms of leukemia to receive lifesaving treatments.

While major cancer centers can quickly diagnose acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL) and chronic myeloid leukemia (CML), most hospitals must send blood samples to centralized labs and wait days or a week for results.

“It doesn’t matter if you have highly effective treatment for a disease if you can’t diagnose that disease,” said R. Coleman Lindsley, MD, PhD, director of the Edward P. Evans Center for MDS at Dana-Farber and senior author of the research published in Blood in 2024. “Patients who develop APL are at a high risk of death from bleeding if treatment isn’t begun promptly. With our test, an emergency room physician could know within a couple of hours if the patient should receive a medication that immediately reverses the risk of bleeding.”

The Institute’s Robert and Renée Belfer Center for Applied Cancer Science is working to develop the technology into a commercial product.

jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: When The Dana-Farber Campaign was announced in 2021, cancer early detection and interception represented a key priority to re-imagine cancer care and it remains so today.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Priscilla Lawrence and Patrick MeLampy
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A new $1 million gift from Rev. Dr. Priscilla Lawrence and Patrick MeLampy will advance the work of Irene Ghobrial, MD, a Lavine Family Chair for Preventative Cancer Therapies at Dana-Farber, and the Center for Early Detection and Interception of Blood Cancers to better understand risk factors for multiple myeloma…

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On Sept. 30, Dana-Farber announced the completion of one of the largest-ever fundraising campaigns focused solely on cancer: The Dana-Farber Campaign.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Cancer Prevention Initiative
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Cancer Prevention Initiative (CPI) awarded $450,000 to Kornelia Polyak, MD, PhD, for her breast cancer research at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, targeting early tumor progression. This grant highlights CPI’s vital support for and shared mission with Dana-Farber in advancing impactful strategies for early medical interception of inherited cancer to improve…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Paving the way to cancer prevention
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Wycliffe “Wyc” Grousbeck and Emilia Fazzalari are firm believers that “good things don’t come easy.” As philanthropic and entrepreneurial leaders in the Boston community, they seek out innovative and exceptional people who are tackling groundbreaking endeavors that are simply too compelling to refuse.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign: Join Us
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With three months remaining in The Dana-Farber Campaign, there is still time to join us in this truly historic effort that will forever change cancer research and care.

title.rendered: The Dana-Farber Campaign: The promise of personalized cancer vaccines

content.rendered:
Spring 2025
By Kathy Clute
Photography by Sam Ogden

Funds raised through The Dana-Farber Campaign are speeding our efforts to amplify the powerful benefits of immunotherapies, including a vaccine developed by Institute scientists that harnesses the body’s immune system to attack cancerous cells. This personalized cancer vaccine, called NeoVax, has been effective in melanoma patients and is now being studied for its potential to defeat other cancers.

NeoVax works by targeting the unique mutations in a patient’s tumor. After genetic sequencing identifies specific neoantigens—proteins formed by the mutations—scientists use copies of them to create a personalized vaccine. The vaccine trains the body’s immune system to seek out and destroy cells displaying the neoantigens while leaving normal ones intact.

The technology is so promising that Dana-Farber established the Center for Cancer Vaccines in 2020, led by the vaccine’s developers, Catherine Wu, MD, Lavine Family Chair for Preventative Cancer Therapies at Dana-Farber, and Patrick Ott, MD, PhD.

Wu and other Dana-Farber researchers are now investigating whether NeoVax, paired with additional medicines, might be effective against chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL), high-risk renal cell carcinoma, glioblastoma, and ovarian cancer. They are also working to develop AMPVax (Artificial Mini-Proteome Vaccine), a next-generation cancer vaccine that overcomes two current barriers to widespread NeoVax use: production costs and time.

title.rendered: The Dana-Farber Campaign: New initiative enhances nursing care

content.rendered:
Spring 2025
By Kathy Clute
Photography by Sasha Pedro

Thanks to the support of The Dana-Farber Campaign, the Institute has launched an ambitious program to enhance the patient experience and boost clinical innovation in nursing. The Ning Zhao & Ge Li Family Initiative in Nursing will strengthen the education and training of oncology nurses through research, innovation, and professional development while building a pipeline of highly trained oncology nurses for the future.

The initiative will also include a state-of-the-art simulation center where nurses can receive hands-on training in a facility that replicates the clinical environment. The center, expected to open in 2025, will prepare nurses with key technical skills, such as starting IVs, administering chemotherapy, and practicing for emergency scenarios.

“Nurses need specific competencies and clinical expertise in caring for patients with cancer,” said Anne Gross, PhD, RN, FAAN, the Ning Zhao Chair of Nursing at Dana-Farber. “By enhancing our training and professional development programs, we ensure that we can continue to provide the highest quality care while maximizing each patient’s quality of life during treatment.”

title.rendered: The Dana-Farber Campaign: FDA approves new pediatric brain cancer drug

content.rendered:
Spring 2025
By Kathy Clute
Photography by John Deputy

Gifts to The Dana-Farber Campaign accelerated efforts in our laboratories to find new measures to prevent and treat cancer, lessen the side effects of therapies, and stop every childhood cancer in its tracks. Dana-Farber research led to U.S. Food and Drug Administration approval in 2024 of a new medicine for children with the most common form of pediatric brain cancer.

The oral medication, tovorafenib, is for young patients with relapsed or progressive pediatric low-grade glioma, which is diagnosed in about 3,000 children in the U.S. each year. Standard treatments often leave these patients with lifelong neurological, hormonal, visual, or other problems, and newer treatments have been urgently needed to help those children survive with fewer long-term side effects.

“This is an example of what Dana-Farber is capable of,” said Karen Wright, MD. “An approval for a pediatric tumor doesn’t happen very often.”

The FDA action came after researchers in Dana-Farber’s Department of Cancer Biology spent more than a decade researching genetic mutations in gliomas. After their preclinical work proved that tovorafenib penetrated the blood-brain barrier and shut down a protein that was causing the cancer cells to grow unchecked, the FDA declared it a “breakthrough therapy” in 2020. This enabled clinical trials that led to the full approval four years later.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Stop & Shop raises over $760,000 for pediatric cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: This spring, New England Stop & Shop customers donated over $760,000 to pediatric cancer research at Dana-Farber through the grocery chain’s annual Help Cure Childhood Cancer campaign.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign: Closing the equity gap in cancer care
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Funds from The Dana-Farber Campaign allow us to expand access to underserved populations and improve research to reduce disparities in treatment outcomes.

img.alt_text: Patient Navigator Judy Thyme, MSPH (left), assists patient Carle Price with her medications.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Stop & Shop raises $1.4 million for pediatric cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: New England Stop & Shop customers donated $1.4 million to pediatric cancer research at Dana-Farber last year during the grocery chain’s 31st annual Help Cure Childhood Cancer campaign, which has raised a total of $77 million for the Institute since 1991.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign
jetpack-related-posts.author: danafarberandthejimmyfund@gmail.com

content.rendered:
Spring 2025
By Kathy Clute
Photography by Bryce Vickmark

The Dana-Farber Campaign raised vital funds to encourage early career investigators to continue their promising research. The Lubin Family Foundation Scholar Award exemplifies the Institute’s commitment to retaining the brightest physician-scientists in academic medicine as they launch their research careers.

Since 2022, Lubin Scholars have been tackling tough questions ranging from genetic vulnerabilities in glioblastoma to how to attack advanced cancers through translational genomics. They are guided and supported by Lubin Scholar Mentors who are senior leaders in the relevant scientific field. In addition, each Lubin Scholar receives four years of financial support for their work.

Many studies have shown that physician-scientists leave academic research early in their careers for reasons including financial limitations and more opportunities in the private sector. Overcoming these formidable barriers to retention is critical to the future of Dana-Farber’s research enterprise.

“Lubin Scholars are all on their way to becoming next-generation leaders in their fields,” said Nobel Laureate William G. Kaelin Jr., MD, the program’s scientific director and the Sidney Farber Professor of Medicine. “They can benefit from the same kind of transformative mentoring I got from the late Dr. David Livingston as they face the many choices and decisions that will shape their careers.”

excerpt.rendered: The Dana-Farber Campaign established 49 new endowed positions, including support for early career investigators.

title.rendered: The Dana-Farber Campaign: A future of possibilities

content.rendered:
Spring 2025
By Kathy Clute
Photography by John Deputy

Looking forward and building on the momentum of The Dana-Farber Campaign’s community of support, we see so much that makes us hopeful. Data science and artificial intelligence make it possible to understand the underpinnings of cancer and develop targeted therapies to defeat it. Liquid biopsies offer ways to detect tumor DNA in the blood before any symptoms of disease appear. Immunotherapies catalyze the body’s own immune system to attack and kill cancerous cells.

But an estimated 40% of Americans will develop cancer in their lifetimes, and we recognize that more people will need advanced cancer care than ever before. We believe that the best place to deliver that care is in a setting solely dedicated to treating people with cancer.

Dana-Farber’s vision is to center the patient, family, and caregiver experience, expand access to value-driven care, and foster scientific discovery. A centerpiece of this vision will be achieved through a proposed future cancer hospital, subject to regulatory approvals. To learn more about our plans to transform cancer care, visit Dana-Farber.org.

We’ve come so far because of you, our dedicated supporters, and your continued support will spark important discoveries, enhance patient care and outcomes, and influence the lives of children and adults with cancer for years to come. We look forward to your partnership as we move into a future full of possibilities.

excerpt.rendered: More people will need advanced cancer care than ever before, and the best place to deliver that care is in a setting solely dedicated to treating people with cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On Sept. 30, Dana-Farber announced the completion of one of the largest-ever fundraising campaigns focused solely on cancer: The Dana-Farber Campaign.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Data science and AI allow us to better match patients to clinical trials, identify disparities in cancer care, and pinpoint the most promising treatment options.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign
jetpack-related-posts.author: danafarberandthejimmyfund@gmail.com
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Establishing an endowment is a powerful way to support The Dana-Farber Campaign.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign: Join Us
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With three months remaining in The Dana-Farber Campaign, there is still time to join us in this truly historic effort that will forever change cancer research and care.

img.alt_text: Dana-Farber Trustees Monica Chandra and Michael Eisenson in the hospital's healing garden

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber Presidential Symposium
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: “Sparking Discoveries Through the Power of Community” was the theme for the annual Dana-Farber Cancer Institute Presidential Symposium in October 2023

img.alt_text: A photo of two people sitting in chairs

jetpack-related-posts.title: Hazel B. Harrington Trust
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Hazel B. Harrington Trust has made a generous gift of $124,668 to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. This contribution, reflecting Ms. Harrington’s foresight and commitment, supports the Institute’s efforts to develop innovative cancer treatments and expand access to care. Her legacy significantly impacts patient lives and advances The Dana-Farber Campaign mission.

content.rendered:
Spring 2025
Photography by Josh Campbell

Dana-Farber Cancer Institute is deeply grateful to the members of the Campaign Cabinet, who wholeheartedly devoted their time, talents, and resources to advancing The Dana-Farber Campaign’s mission to Defy Cancer.

Michael Eisenson, Chair
Monica Chandra, Vice Chair
Laurie H. Glimcher, MD
Josh Bekenstein
Jane Brock-Wilson
David Dechman
Phill Gross
Michele Kessler
Phyllis Krock
Jeannie and Jonathan Lavine
Richard Lubin
Larry Lucchino ∞
James McCann
Karen Linde Packman
Barrett J. Rollins, MD, PhD
Barbara and Jim Sadowsky
Eric Schlager
Billy Starr
Beth Terrana

∞ Deceased

jetpack-related-posts.title: Palm Beach surpasses $67 million in gifts to The Dana-Farber Campaign
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For over three decades, the compassionate community in Palm Beach, Florida, has provided generous support for Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s lifesaving mission to conquer cancer in adults and children—not only in Boston and Palm Beach, but also across the country and around the world.

img.alt_text: Dana-Farber Palm Beach Campaign Leadership Celebration Dinner

jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact

jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact

content.rendered:
Spring 2025
By Casey Repasy

A Chance for Kids & Families raised over $425,000 in 2024 for cancer research and patient care at Dana-Farber. Patrons who donate to the Jimmy Fund at participating Burger King®, The Paper Store®, and Valvoline Instant Oil ChangeSM locations receive coupons, with all proceeds supporting Dana-Farber’s lifesaving mission.

content.rendered:
Spring 2025
By Stephanie Lowitt
Photography by Michael Blanchard

The American Heart Association awarded $147,000 to research fellow Jee Hyung Sohn, PhD, for her work exploring how increasing the ability of mitochondria (which generate most of a cell’s chemical energy) to burn energy in brown and beige fat cells could reduce the incidence of heart and blood vessel disease.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Mathers Foundation grants promote basic cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Many of today’s important advances in cancer care trace their origins to basic research—a form of scientific investigation aimed at uncovering the fundamental principles of biology, chemistry, and foundational science.

jetpack-related-posts.title: AACR grants support sarcoma, renal cell carcinoma, and cancer biology research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Association for Cancer Research (AACR) recently awarded $580,000 to three Dana-Farber physician-scientists who are investigating new methods of prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of various types of cancers. As the first cancer research organization dedicated to preventing and curing cancer, AACR is a long-standing partner in Dana-Farber’s mission to…

jetpack-related-posts.title: AACR targets breast and uterine cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Association for Cancer Research recently awarded more than $1 million in grants to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute investigators.

jetpack-related-posts.title: American Gastroenterological Association
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Gastroenterological Association awarded $300,000 to support a Dana-Farber study into pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), an aggressive disease that currently has limited and short-lasting treatment options. This funding will enable Jeffrey Patterson-Fortin, MD, PhD, to gain insights into how PDAC responds to immune-based therapies that could provide longer term…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Cancer Research Institute invests in the people behind basic research discoveries in cancer immunology
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: While the immune system is inherently able to identify and destroy harmful cells, tumors often develop ways to interrupt anti-cancer immune activity. Restoring this powerful effect in order to defeat cancer through therapies that galvanize the immune system has transformed the treatment trajectory and potential for cure in many cancers.

jetpack-related-posts.title: American Brain Tumor Association
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With a grant of $100,000 from the American Brain Tumor Association, Jun Nishida, PhD, is studying the drivers of brain metastases in breast cancer. By researching how varying nutrient levels in different parts of the brain select cancer cells, the team hopes to identify new therapeutic targets in order to…

Spring 2025
By Bethany Herrema
Photography by Jessamyn Martin

The Anna Fuller Fund has made a wonderful impact with a $150,000 gift to support breast cancer research conducted by Evanna Mills, PhD, at Dana-Farber. The investment will fuel investigations to better understand risk factors for triple-negative breast cancer with the potential to inform the development of more effective treatments.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Pew Charitable Trusts
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Pew Charitable Trusts provided $430,000 in support of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute researchers Evanna Mills, PhD, and Brenda Nakagaki, PhD. The investment will fuel investigations into how metabolic dysfunction impacts immune cell function, particularly macrophages, and triggers harmful inflammation in different cells and tissues.

jetpack-related-posts.title: William and Barbara Connolly
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s Sara M. Tolaney, MD, MPH, received a $100,000 gift from the Connolly Family Fund, established by William and Barbara Connolly, to advance innovative breast cancer research. Their support empowers Tolaney’s team to develop novel strategies for early detection, prevention, and personalized treatment, helping to improve outcomes for…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Michael Swidler
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute received a gracious contribution from Michael Swidler to establish the Nancy Swidler Fund for Breast Cancer Research in honor of his late wife. Managed by Sara Tolaney, MD, MPH, this fund is intended to advance pioneering breast cancer research and create pathways to better outcomes for every…

jetpack-related-posts.title: American Cancer Society targets improved treatments and access
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Cancer Society (ACS) recently awarded $1.12 million in grants to four Dana-Farber researchers seeking to answer those questions and more.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Karen O’Connor and Bruce MacGregor
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Karen O’Connor and Bruce MacGregor renewed their support for the O’Connor-MacGregor Fund for Melanoma Research with a new $150,000 commitment. This latest gift will support research into the underlying drivers of melanoma and development of durable therapeutic options under the direction of Rizwan Haq, MD, PhD.

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Legacy of Leadership and Hope: The Elaine and Eduardo Saverin Foundation’s generational commitment to patients with metastatic breast cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Elaine and Eduardo Saverin Foundation has made an extraordinary $20 million grant to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute to accelerate research and care for people living with stage IV breast cancer.

Spring 2025
By Ross Perry
Photography by Josh Campbell

The Estate of Carolyn Brophy has generously bequeathed $120,697.36 to support cancer research and care at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. Carolyn’s commitment to Dana-Farber’s mission will drive promising research and innovative treatments. Her legacy will inspire breakthroughs and improve patient experiences, helping Dana-Farber continue to defy cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Hazel B. Harrington Trust
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Hazel B. Harrington Trust has made a generous gift of $124,668 to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. This contribution, reflecting Ms. Harrington’s foresight and commitment, supports the Institute’s efforts to develop innovative cancer treatments and expand access to care. Her legacy significantly impacts patient lives and advances The Dana-Farber Campaign mission.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Palm Beach community rallies to surpass annual fundraising goal
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Palm Beach community once again demonstrated remarkable generosity by raising over $1.31 million to support Dana-Farber Cancer Institute through their Palm Beach Annual appeal.

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Legacy of Leadership and Hope: The Elaine and Eduardo Saverin Foundation’s generational commitment to patients with metastatic breast cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Elaine and Eduardo Saverin Foundation has made an extraordinary $20 million grant to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute to accelerate research and care for people living with stage IV breast cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Society
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Dana-Farber Society (DFS) is a group of visionary donors who are changing lives and creating a legacy through a planned gift such as a bequest, life income gift, or beneficiary designation to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, the Jimmy Fund, the Friends of Dana-Farber, or the Pan-Mass Challenge.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Friends of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Friends of Dana-Farber hosted a variety of events throughout 2024 that raised more than $600,000 for lifesaving cancer research and patient care.

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Message from Melany Duval
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dear friends, Every day our philanthropic community supports a relentless commitment to possibilities in cancer care at Dana-Farber—and that gives me hope.

Spring 2025
By Ross Perry
Photography by Bryce Vickmark

The Estate of Ruth F. Byrne made a generous gift of $442,698 to the Jimmy Fund of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. Mrs. Byrne’s gift makes a profound difference and propels our relentless determination to revolutionize cancer science, pioneer world-class cancer care, and increase access to cancer treatments for all.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Freedlander bequest focuses on inflammatory breast cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The estate of Ruth Freedlander made a $1.8 million bequest to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute that will advance research into inflammatory breast cancer (IBC), a rare and aggressive disease that is particularly difficult to treat.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Estate gift accelerates cancer care and research for years to come
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Out of gratitude for the excellent care received by his late wife, Gerry Martineau left a generous bequest to support research and patient care at Dana-Farber.

img.alt_text: Steaming beaker and pipette in the lab

jetpack-related-posts.title: Eisenson encourages CGAs as a simple and lasting legacy
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Supporting cancer research and care at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute can take many forms that benefit both the Institute and the donor. Michael Eisenson (pictured), Institute Trustee and chair of The Dana-Farber Campaign, recently established a charitable gift annuity (CGA) with a generous gift of $250,000.

img.alt_text: Michael Eisenson at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute's healing garden

jetpack-related-posts.title: Robert Rosenthal Estate
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The estate of Robert Rosenthal, PhD, known as a father of meta-analysis and one of the 20th century's top 100 psychologists, left a $174,000 gift to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. He had a special devotion to research and patient care, which are the areas this gift will support.

content.rendered:
Spring 2025
By Samantha Sullivan

The Cancer Couch Foundation recently made a gift of $125,000 to support metastatic breast cancer (MBC) research under the direction of Daniel Abravanel, MD, PhD. This gift enables Abravanel and his team to leverage cutting-edge profiling technologies, such as single-cell sequencing and spatial profiling, to develop personalized and effective treatments to combat MBC.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Cancer Couch Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Cancer Couch Foundation has granted $225,000 to support the work of Daniel Abravanel, MD, PhD. The funds will drive Abravanel’s research on how drug resistance arises in metastatic breast cancer and foster the development of innovative strategies for improving treatments for patients with this challenging form of the disease.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Donor bequeaths $1 million gift to metastatic breast cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Through an estate provision added to her will, Anne P. Olsen has bequeathed $1 million to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. The gift will be directed to the Hilary J. Olsen Fund for Metastatic Breast Cancer, which was established in 2019 by Anne’s son, Jeff. The fund is in memory of Jeff’s…

jetpack-related-posts.title: METAvivor advances metastatic breast cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: METAvivor has awarded three grants totaling $850,000 to advance metastatic breast cancer research at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute.

jetpack-related-posts.title: METAvivor advances metastatic breast cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: METAvivor, a non-profit organization that funds important research for stage IV metastatic breast cancer (MBC), has awarded research grants totaling $700,000 to three Dana-Farber faculty members

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Terri Brodeur Breast Cancer Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Terri Brodeur Breast Cancer Foundation gave $125,000 in support of research led by Paolo Tarantino, MD, which seeks to improve the precision of antibody-drug conjugates. This funding will aid Tarantino in unlocking new insights into metastatic breast cancer, with the intention of identifying additional treatments for patients.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Breast Cancer Alliance
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Breast Cancer Alliance awarded $125,000 to Dana-Farber to support research into the features of the tumor microenvironment that result in metastatic triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). This work will improve researchers’ knowledge of the behavior of TNBC and may help identify patients who are more likely to benefit from treatments such…

content.rendered:
Spring 2025
By Kayla McMahon

Siblings Susie Mitchell, Lisa Fideli, and Chuck Martin once again hosted their Derby Day fundraiser in memory of their mother, Sharon Crowley Martin, who passed away from melanoma in 2007. They raised $143,000 to advance the vital research of Dana-Farber’s Sharon Crowley Martin Chair in Melanoma, F. Stephen Hodi Jr., MD.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Martin family’s events surpass $1 million milestone
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In January, Dana-Farber celebrated the more than $1 million cumulatively raised by the family of the late Sharon Crowley Martin through events including Derby Day, a Kentucky Derby-themed cocktail watch party.

img.alt_text: The Martin family receiving an award

jetpack-related-posts.title: Brian and Jane Crowley
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Brian and Jane Crowley gave $100,000 to support the work of F. Stephan Hodi Jr., MD, director of the Melanoma Center and the Sharon Crowley Martin Chair in Melanoma at Dana-Farber. Bolstered by this generous funding, Hodi is pursuing innovative research into new therapeutic approaches for melanoma.

jetpack-related-posts.title: John Cassidy
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: John Cassidy’s generous $300,000 gift establishes the Cassidy Family Melanoma Fellowship, to significantly advance melanoma research. Under the guidance of principal investigator F. Stephen Hodi Jr., MD, the Sharon Crowley Martin Chair in Melanoma at Dana-Farber, this funding will help support the mentorship of an early career investigator, fostering innovation…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Robinson Family
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Robinson Family established the memorial Lena Maximo Robinson Fund with a $100,000 gift, supporting the melanoma research of F. Stephen Hodi Jr., MD, the Sharon Crowley Martin Chair in Melanoma at Dana-Farber. With these funds, Hodi’s team will continue their leadership in developing next-generation, cutting-edge treatments for all subtypes…

img.alt_text: Lena Maximo Robinson and Richard Robinson.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Melanoma Research Alliance advances personalized immunotherapies
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A $900,000 Team Science grant will advance collaboration and innovation in immunotherapies for melanoma at Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Malcolm and Luli MacNaught
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With a recent gift of $100,000, Malcolm and Luli MacNaught continued their steadfast support for Dana-Farber’s F. Stephen Hodi Jr., MD, a pioneer in groundbreaking treatments for melanoma. Among these is the recent trial of a new combination of immune checkpoint inhibitors that allowed patients with metastatic melanoma to survive…

content.rendered:
Spring 2025
By Lori Dougherty

Carla L. DeSantis established the Robert A. DeSantis Fund for Cancer Research with a gift of $150,000 in memory of her father. With this investment, Brian Wolpin, MD, and his team in the Gastrointestinal Cancer Center are well-positioned to design new clinical trials with the goal of developing more effective therapies for patients with pancreatic and colon cancers.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Julie Wallace Bennett
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With a $250,000 gift, Julie Wallace Bennett established the Peter Warren Fund for Pancreatic Research, in honor of her partner, Peter. Brian Wolpin, MD, MPH, the Robert T. and Judith B. Hale Chair in Pancreatic Cancer at Dana-Farber will lead this research.

img.alt_text: A photo of a couple in front of a body water

jetpack-related-posts.title: Gift continues donor’s legacy by supporting gastrointestinal research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Throughout her life, Ilene Beal was dedicated to hard work and breaking down barriers. She became a female pioneer in the Boston banking world and was a valued mentor for other women in the industry.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Phillips Family
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: George Phillips, together with his daughters, Kimberly and Jill, established the Juliana M. Phillips Fund Accelerating Cancer Research in honor of his late wife, Juliana, with a $150,000 gift. The fund will offer essential financial support for research into pancreatic, esophageal, gastric, and other gastrointestinal cancers, under the leadership of…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Ilene Beal Charitable Foundation gift focuses on cancer interception
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A $1.25 million gift to Dana-Farber from the Ilene Beal Charitable Foundation supports research focused on ways pancreatic cancer might be detected—and intercepted—before it can be seen on CT scans or other imaging modalities.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Lustgarten grant accelerates therapeutic discovery in pancreatic cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Lustgarten Foundation is the largest private funder of pancreatic cancer research in the world, funding preeminent pancreatic cancer researchers, driving the pursuit of bold and innovative science toward earlier detection and better treatments, and transforming pancreatic cancer into a curable disease.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Hale Family receives the Sidney Farber Medical Research Award
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In November 2023, Dana-Farber Trustee Judy Hale, Dana-Farber Trustee Karen Hale, Rob Hale, Elizabeth Hale Kendall, and Richard Kendall were awarded the Sidney Farber Medical Research Award in recognition of the Hale Family’s outstanding contributions and service to the Institute for many decades.

jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber is committed to providing the best possible care to patients from all walks of life. In recent years, the Institute has prioritized expanding its clinical facilities into surrounding communities to better reach medically underserved patients with the Institute’s signature Total Patient Care model, which includes supportive services from the…

img.alt_text: Alison Poorvu Jaffe and Daniel G. Jaffe

jetpack-related-posts.title: Poorvu Jaffe Chair Celebration
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: James Tulsky, MD, was named the first incumbent of the Poorvu Jaffe Chair in Psychosocial Oncology and Palliative Care at Dana-Farber, the first chair in this field established at the Institute. The Poorvu Jaffe Family’s gift also established the Poorvu Jaffe Fund for Supportive Oncology and Health Equity. Pictured at…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Robert Cummins
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Robert Cummins gave $100,000 to establish The Deborah Cummins Waldenström’s Memorial Fund in honor of his late wife. Cummins’ investment is enabling a team at Dana-Farber’s Bing Center for Waldenström’s Macroglobulinemia to lead clinical trials that are pivotal in the development of more durable, effective treatments.

jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dr. Gerald and Mrs. Mary McGillicuddy made a $100,000 gift to support the work of Julia Rotow, MD, a researcher in the Lowe Center for Thoracic Oncology at Dana-Farber. With this gift, Rotow and her team will work to develop better, more effective targeted and immunotherapy options for patients with…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Michael and Margaret Kerr
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Michael and Margaret Kerr established the Kerr Family Fund for Translational Research at Dana-Farber with a $100,000 gift in 2023. The fund will be directed by James Cleary, MD, PhD, whom the couple laud for his compassionate patient care.

content.rendered:
Spring 2025
By Bethany Herrema
Photography by Sam Ogden

The Gordon and Betty Moore Foundation gave $149,923 to accelerate research led by Betsy O’Donnell, MD, at Dana-Farber. “We seek to support durable change guided by science to positively impact the most people possible,” says foundation President Harvey Fineberg, PhD, of their investment to drive discovery for patients facing hematologic diseases.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Paving the way to cancer prevention
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Wycliffe “Wyc” Grousbeck and Emilia Fazzalari are firm believers that “good things don’t come easy.” As philanthropic and entrepreneurial leaders in the Boston community, they seek out innovative and exceptional people who are tackling groundbreaking endeavors that are simply too compelling to refuse.

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Legacy of Leadership and Hope: The Elaine and Eduardo Saverin Foundation’s generational commitment to patients with metastatic breast cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Elaine and Eduardo Saverin Foundation has made an extraordinary $20 million grant to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute to accelerate research and care for people living with stage IV breast cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In September, the inaugural David Liposarcoma Research Initiative International Scientific Symposium was held at Dana-Farber. The symposium included the unveiling of a plaque commemorating the generous pledge from the Rossy Foundation that, through The Rossy Foundation Fund at KBF Canada, established the David Liposarcoma Research Initiative under the direction of…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Expect Miracles Foundation invests $1.1 million to accelerate cancer breakthroughs at the Belfer Center
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For more than 25 years, Expect Miracles Foundation has united leaders across the financial services industry and beyond to advance life-saving cancer research and support those impacted by the disease.

img.alt_text: Expect Miracles Foundation employees with a large check

jetpack-related-posts.title: Expect Miracles Foundation continues to drive discovery
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For the 29th year, Expect Miracles Foundation reaffirmed their support of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute with a gift of $1 million.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Expect Miracles Foundation raises record $1.25 million
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A dedicated supporter of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute for more than 28 years, Expect Miracles Foundation marked a record-breaking year in 2022 by raising $1.25 million in support of the Robert and Renée Belfer Center for Applied Cancer Science at Dana-Farber.

img.alt_text: Expect Miracles Foundation with large check for Dana-Farber

Spring 2025
By Ross Perry
Photography by Michael Blanchard

The Hazel B. Harrington Trust has made a generous gift of $124,668 to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. This contribution, reflecting Ms. Harrington’s foresight and commitment, supports the Institute’s efforts to develop innovative cancer treatments and expand access to care. Her legacy significantly impacts patient lives and advances The Dana-Farber Campaign mission.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Estate of Serena M. Hatch
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Estate of Serena M. Hatch has made an impactful contribution of $100,000 to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, leaving a lasting legacy in the battle against cancer. Her foresight and generosity empower Dana-Farber to tackle cancer’s toughest challenges and make a meaningful difference in the lives of patients everywhere.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Eisenson encourages CGAs as a simple and lasting legacy
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Supporting cancer research and care at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute can take many forms that benefit both the Institute and the donor. Michael Eisenson (pictured), Institute Trustee and chair of The Dana-Farber Campaign, recently established a charitable gift annuity (CGA) with a generous gift of $250,000.

img.alt_text: Michael Eisenson at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute's healing garden

jetpack-related-posts.title: Steve and Anne Dodge Trust brings family’s long-term commitment full circle
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A generous gift from the trust of the late Steve and Anne Dodge will provide unrestricted support to Dana-Farber.

img.alt_text: Liquid pouring from a beaker into a petri dish

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Hale Family receives the Sidney Farber Medical Research Award
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In November 2023, Dana-Farber Trustee Judy Hale, Dana-Farber Trustee Karen Hale, Rob Hale, Elizabeth Hale Kendall, and Richard Kendall were awarded the Sidney Farber Medical Research Award in recognition of the Hale Family’s outstanding contributions and service to the Institute for many decades.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Estate gift accelerates cancer care and research for years to come
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Out of gratitude for the excellent care received by his late wife, Gerry Martineau left a generous bequest to support research and patient care at Dana-Farber.

img.alt_text: Steaming beaker and pipette in the lab

jetpack-related-posts.title: TA Associates
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: TA Associates made a generous, unrestricted gift of $170,000 to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. Their vital support empowers the Institute to advance cancer research and patient care, fostering innovation and expanding access to treatment. TA's flexible commitment plays a crucial role in driving progress and improving outcomes for patients and families.

Spring 2025
By Ross Perry
Photography by Josh Campbell

The Estate of Serena M. Hatch has made an impactful contribution of $100,000 to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, leaving a lasting legacy in the battle against cancer. Her foresight and generosity empower Dana-Farber to tackle cancer’s toughest challenges and make a meaningful difference in the lives of patients everywhere.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Hazel B. Harrington Trust
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Hazel B. Harrington Trust has made a generous gift of $124,668 to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. This contribution, reflecting Ms. Harrington’s foresight and commitment, supports the Institute’s efforts to develop innovative cancer treatments and expand access to care. Her legacy significantly impacts patient lives and advances The Dana-Farber Campaign mission.

img.alt_text: Liquid pouring from a beaker into a petri dish

jetpack-related-posts.title: Endowed fellowship looks to the future
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Baila Janock embodies generosity in its many forms. For over 30 years, she has combined her gifts of time, treasure, and talent to make a long-lasting impact on Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and its patients.

img.alt_text: Robert Mayer, MD, Baila Janock, and Janock Fellow Haley Ellis, MD

jetpack-related-posts.title: Estate of Carolyn Brophy
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Estate of Carolyn Brophy has generously bequeathed $120,697.36 to support cancer research and care at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. Carolyn’s commitment to Dana-Farber’s mission will drive promising research and innovative treatments. Her legacy will inspire breakthroughs and improve patient experiences, helping Dana-Farber continue to defy cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber Society reaches 2,000 members
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Dana-Farber Society honor those who have made a legacy gift, helping to secure future progress for Dana-Farber research and care.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Anthony Sordillo leaves legacy of generosity
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Former Dana-Farber anesthesiologist Anthony Sordillo left a generous unrestricted bequest to advance our lifesaving mission.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Estate gift accelerates cancer care and research for years to come
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Out of gratitude for the excellent care received by his late wife, Gerry Martineau left a generous bequest to support research and patient care at Dana-Farber.

img.alt_text: Steaming beaker and pipette in the lab

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Herb Chambers Companies surpasses $1 million in gifts
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Herb Chambers Companies, one of New England’s largest auto dealers, has been a powerful ally and supporter of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund since 2015.

img.alt_text: Herb Chambers and his partner, Melissa Lees, with the cow she created, Chin Up, during the CowParade New England Preview Party.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Two longstanding supporters receive the Jimmy Fund’s highest honor
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The 2024 Boston Red Sox Jimmy Fund Award was presented to The Herb Chambers Companies and Team Beans at a special Fenway Park ceremony.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Arbella plays an MVP role in the Jimmy Fund’s mission to strike out cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A longtime partner of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund, Arbella Insurance Group continued its steadfast support of Dana-Farber’s mission throughout 2023, living out the company’s motto of: “Here. For Good.”

img.alt_text: A group of people holding an over-sized check at Fenway Park

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Scooper Bowl® presented by Herb Chambers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Over three sunny days in June, more than 10,000 enthusiasts gathered to enjoy unlimited ice cream, with proceeds supporting Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: CowParade New England MOOves the needle
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The cows of CowParade New England presented by Herb Chambers are MOOving to new pastures after a successful, summer-long event celebrating the Jimmy Fund’s 75th anniversary with the Greater Boston community.

img.alt_text: People pose with colorful umbrellas and a dog in front of a painted cow sculpture

jetpack-related-posts.title: Milestone 20th annual WEEI/NESN Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon raises $3.5 million
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Since 1953, the Boston Red Sox have had a deep and multifaceted impact on patients with cancer through its strong partnership with Dana-Farber and the Jimmy Fund.

img.alt_text: Dana-Farber patient and doctor on the field at Fenway Park
