Spring 2025
By Bethany Herrema

Mohammad Rashidian, PhD, received The International Myeloma Society and Paula and Rodger Riney Foundation Translational Research Award. He will use his $250,000 grant to empower investigations to address the challenge of disease relapse in patients treated with a specific type of CAR T-cell therapy. Such studies hold great promise in extending the efficacy of this treatment option.

jetpack-related-posts.title: International Myeloma Society
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s Mohammad Rashidian, PhD, received a $250,000 Translational Research Award from the International Myeloma Society and the Paula and Rodger Riney Foundation. This support will advance his innovative work to combat disease relapse in multiple myeloma patients following CAR T-cell therapy.

jetpack-related-posts.title: IMS grants drive innovative multiple myeloma research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The International Myeloma Society (IMS) recently awarded three Dana-Farber scientists grants totaling $525,000 to promote research on the blood cancer multiple myeloma.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Paula and Rodger Riney Foundation sustains momentum in multiple myeloma research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Multiple myeloma treatments have significantly improved over the past two decades, thanks in part to the driving engine of transformational philanthropy.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Leukemia & Lymphoma Society grants target blood cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Leukemia & Lymphoma Society recently awarded more than $7.3 million in grants to Dana-Farber researchers in its quest to better understand and find cures for blood cancers.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Leukemia & Lymphoma Society attacks rare and resistant blood cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Leukemia & Lymphoma Society (LLS) has awarded six grants totaling $5.8 million to Dana-Farber investigators.

img.alt_text: An artist’s rendering of bone marrow cells showing acute myeloid leukemia.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Gift honors late wife and supports multiple myeloma research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Kenneth Nirenstein remembers his late wife, Harriet, as wise, elegant, and graceful. After Harriet’s passing, seeking a way to keep her memory alive while also making a difference to others, Kenneth made a gift of $100,000 to establish the Harriet Shapiro Nirenstein Fund for Multiple Myeloma Research at Dana-Farber.

img.alt_text: A photo of a couple in front of an ocean

content.rendered:
Spring 2025
By Lori Dougherty
Photography by Jessamyn Martin

With a gift of $100,000, Arthur David Levin established the Andrew John Torino Fund for Esophageal Cancer in honor of a dear friend’s husband, Andrew. This fund will advance the development of a new test to detect circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) in the blood, with the goal of determining the risk of cancer recurrence in esophageal cancer patients after surgery.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Chubb gift advances ctDNA research for cancer detection and therapies
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With a $750,000 gift, Patricia and Steve Chubb established The Alice Fund to support Parsons’ research into ctDNA and her lab’s efforts to develop technologies to overcome current limitations.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Innovation in Cancer Informatics
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Innovation in Cancer Informatics awarded $224,000 to support investigations led by Sylvan Baca, MD, PhD, and Eliezer Van Allen, MD, into circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA). This research will analyze tumor features and aims to, for the first time, guide therapy selection in breast cancer with low levels of ctDNA.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Little Warrior Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Little Warrior Foundation has granted $100,000 to Brian Crompton, MD, to develop a CLIA/CAP-certified pediatric-specific circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) assay. This non-invasive test aims to detect pediatric-specific cancer mutations that will be helpful in monitoring treatment response and may one day allow for risk stratification at diagnosis—helping clinicians tailor treatment…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Phillips Family
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: George Phillips, together with his daughters, Kimberly and Jill, established the Juliana M. Phillips Fund Accelerating Cancer Research in honor of his late wife, Juliana, with a $150,000 gift. The fund will offer essential financial support for research into pancreatic, esophageal, gastric, and other gastrointestinal cancers, under the leadership of…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Lee and Alexandria Zachos
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Lee and Alexandria Zachos made a gift of $100,000 to The Vasilios Kafkes Fund for Pediatric Cancer Research II at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, supporting Brian Crompton, MD, to advance ctDNA testing in pediatric tumors–a noninvasive blood test to improve detection, prevention, and care in childhood cancers–by developing a clinical assay…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Clifford Family
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Clifford Family established the Woolley-Clifford Foundation Fund with a $100,000 gift, supporting the research of David Kozono, MD, PhD, as he works to investigate blood and tissue-based biomarkers in lung cancer patients that can help predict lung inflammation and anti-tumor response following radiation therapy.

Spring 2025
By Kayla McMahon

Jimmy Fund Little League presented by Franklin Sports raised more than $272,000 for Dana-Farber in its 39th season. New England’s young baseball and softball players extended their Little League® seasons to take a swing at cancer by raising vital funds for cancer research and care at Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Little League
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Jimmy Fund Little League presented by Franklin Sports raised $281,332 in 2023 for cancer research and care at Dana-Farber. Every year, Little League baseball and softball players in New England raise vital funds for the Jimmy Fund during this summer league, making a significant impact in the fight against cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Boston Red Sox Jimmy Fund Award
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The 2022 Boston Red Sox Jimmy Fund Award—the Jimmy Fund’s highest honor—was presented to John Berardi (second from right), program director of Jimmy Fund Little League presented by Franklin Sports, which rallies thousands of youth baseball and softball players each summer to fundraise for the Jimmy Fund in their communities…

img.alt_text: People on the field at Fenway Park

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Little League
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Jimmy Fund Little League presented by the Yawkey Foundation surpassed its $275,000 goal, contributing $359,476 of unrestricted funding to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and underscoring the Yawkey Foundation’s dedication to advancing care for its community. The top fundraising team was North Reading 10U Gold, raising $18,465, and the top individual fundraiser, James Keohan, raised $10,617.

img.alt_text: Jimmy Fund Little League presented by Yawkey Foundation

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Golf community helps to usher in the Jimmy Fund’s 75th
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Jimmy Fund Golf presented by Mohegan Sun marked another ace year in 2023, with an array of dedicated tournament directors, sponsors, and supporters across the country raising more than $6.8 million for The Dana-Farber Campaign.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Red Sox name 2023 Jimmy Fund Captain
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Boston Red Sox pitcher, Garrett Whitlock, has been named Jimmy Fund Captain for the 2023 baseball season.

img.alt_text: Jimmy Fund Captain Garrett Whitlock in the Fenway dugout with pediatric patient Lily

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Golf celebrates 40 years of defying cancer from the fairways
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Jimmy Fund Golf presented by Mohegan Sun returned in full force in 2022, with courses around New England and across the country welcoming golfers in support of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund’s lifesaving mission.

Spring 2025
By Stephanie Lowitt

With grants totaling $400,000 from LUNGevity Foundation, Jaclyn LoPiccolo, MD, PhD, is researching prediction of genetic lung cancer risk in people under 45 and how risk factors may guide screening and therapeutic approaches; and Elliot Brea, MD, PhD, is exploring how a modified CAR T-cell therapy may be effective in treating non-small cell lung cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: V Foundation spurs pivotal research aimed at new epigenetic therapies
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The V Foundation is spurring Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s efforts to eradicate difficult-to-treat cancers through recent grants totaling $1.6 million awarded to two Dana-Farber investigators who aim to develop novel treatments known as epigenetic therapies.

jetpack-related-posts.title: National Cancer Center
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: National Cancer Center awarded fellowship grants to Dana-Farber totaling $328,000. One new grant will support Katharina Hoebel, MD, PhD, in developing personalized treatment for non-small cell lung cancer through the use of artificial intelligence. With a second new commitment, Diego Martinez Alonso, PhD, will explore how to utilize CDK4/6 inhibitors…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Groundbreaking studies take aim at disparities and advanced disease
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Prostate Cancer Foundation (PCF) has awarded grants totaling more than $2.3 million to Dana-Farber researchers.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Defeating treatment-resistant lung cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A collaborative, multi-institution team led by Dana-Farber’s David Barbie, MD, received a four-year, $2.5 million grant from the International Association for the Study of Lung Cancer (IASLC) and Lung Cancer Research Foundation (LCRF) for researching a cure for non-small cell lung carcinoma.

img.alt_text: IASLC Lung Cancer Research Foundation logo

jetpack-related-posts.title: Alex’s Lemonade Stand Foundation grants millions to advance childhood cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: It all began over 20 years ago with a simple, yet profound, act of kindness by Alex Scott, a determined little girl with cancer, who held a lemonade stand fundraiser to help other kids like her and inspired countless others to do the same.

jetpack-related-posts.title: American Cancer Society targets improved treatments and access
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Cancer Society (ACS) recently awarded $1.12 million in grants to four Dana-Farber researchers seeking to answer those questions and more.

Spring 2025
By Bethany Herrema

The Lymphoma Research Foundation gave $235,000 to support novel research in lymphoma led by Dana-Farber’s Christine Ryan, MD, and Mwanasha Merrill, MD. Both are focused on better understanding the underlying biology that drives the development and advancement of this disease, information which will translate into the delivery of more effective treatments for patients.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Leukemia & Lymphoma Society grants target blood cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Leukemia & Lymphoma Society recently awarded more than $7.3 million in grants to Dana-Farber researchers in its quest to better understand and find cures for blood cancers.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Lymphoma Research Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: As part of their mission to fund innovative research at top institutions around the country, the Lymphoma Research Foundation’s recent funding cycle included awarding grants totaling $115,000 to fund two Dana-Farber studies into advanced treatment options for patients diagnosed with T-cell lymphoma and mantle cell lymphoma.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Lymphoma Research Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Lymphoma Research Foundation awarded Dana-Farber Cancer Institute's Tianfang Ma, PhD, a generous $195,000 Postdoctoral Fellowship Grant, to bolster his research and growth as an independent investigator. Ma’s work focuses on the tumor immune microenvironment in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma and may help enhance immunotherapy effectiveness and identify predictive markers…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Magda And Gus Mininberg
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Magda and Gus Mininberg have made a generous $200,000 contribution to strengthen the Mininberg Family Fund for Cancer Research and the Mininberg Family Fund for Lymphoma Research, guided by David C. Fisher, MD. Their generosity provides steady, strategic support to Fisher and other Dana-Farber Cancer Institute leaders pursuing better outcomes…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Conquering blood cancers is focus of Blood Cancer United grants
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Each year, nearly 200,000 Americans are diagnosed with leukemia, lymphoma, myeloma, or another bloodborne cancer. Blood Cancer United has awarded $4.2 million in grants to eight Dana-Farber physician-scientists working to better understand, treat, and potentially cure these often deadly diseases.

jetpack-related-posts.title: National Palliative Care Research Center
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The National Palliative Care Research Center awarded $198,000 to support the creation of a program to develop nurse-led psychosocial intervention for historically marginalized pediatric patients, with the goal of improving family-centered communication and pediatric patients’ quality of life during treatment.

Spring 2025
By Kayla McMahon

Kevin and Kimberley Mitnick made a generous gift to support pancreatic cancer research by Srivatsan Raghavan, MD, PhD, before Kevin’s passing from pancreatic cancer in July 2023. This generous contribution reflects their desire to help Dana-Farber uncover new treatment options and improve outcomes for all patients facing pancreatic cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Pancreatic Cancer Action Network
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With their latest commitment of $300,000, the Pancreatic Cancer Action Network is supporting the work of Dana-Farber’s Andrew Aguirre, MD, PhD, who aims to identify the mechanisms of response or resistance to a combination treatment for pancreatic cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Hale Family receives the Sidney Farber Medical Research Award
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In November 2023, Dana-Farber Trustee Judy Hale, Dana-Farber Trustee Karen Hale, Rob Hale, Elizabeth Hale Kendall, and Richard Kendall were awarded the Sidney Farber Medical Research Award in recognition of the Hale Family’s outstanding contributions and service to the Institute for many decades.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Lustgarten grant accelerates therapeutic discovery in pancreatic cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Lustgarten Foundation is the largest private funder of pancreatic cancer research in the world, funding preeminent pancreatic cancer researchers, driving the pursuit of bold and innovative science toward earlier detection and better treatments, and transforming pancreatic cancer into a curable disease.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Pancreatic Cancer Action Network
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Pancreatic Cancer Action Network recently awarded $400,000 in grant funding to Institute researchers Julien Dilly, MS, and William Freed-Pastor, MD, PhD, to better understand mechanisms of response and resistance to KRAS inhibition in pancreatic cancer and improve existing pre-clinical models for this intractable disease.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Novel clinical trial in pancreatic cancer bolstered by $1 million gift
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: John Byrnes is a self-proclaimed “satisfied customer.” Diagnosed with stage IV pancreatic cancer in 2015, John is grateful for each and every day his Dana-Farber care team has given him.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Lustgarten Foundation invests $1.5 million to bring promising immunotherapy to patients with pancreatic cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: When the Lustgarten Foundation was founded in 1998, fewer than 10 principal investigators across the U.S. had a primary focus on pancreatic cancer.

Spring 2025
By Samantha Sullivan

National Cancer Center awarded fellowship grants to Dana-Farber totaling $328,000. One new grant will support Katharina Hoebel, MD, PhD, in developing personalized treatment for non-small cell lung cancer through the use of artificial intelligence. With a second new commitment, Diego Martinez Alonso, PhD, will explore how to utilize CDK4/6 inhibitors as anticancer drugs.

title.rendered: National Comprehensive Cancer Network® (NCCN®) Oncology Research Program

content.rendered:
Spring 2025
By Stephanie Lowitt

The National Comprehensive Cancer Network® (NCCN®) Oncology Research Program awarded $249,999 to Alicia Morgans, MD, MPH, to help assess and manage cardiovascular risk in patients with prostate cancer who are starting androgen deprivation therapy. Her study explores improving patient care in ways that work for clinical teams, are low burden to patients, and are scalable.

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Legacy of Leadership and Hope: The Elaine and Eduardo Saverin Foundation’s generational commitment to patients with metastatic breast cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Elaine and Eduardo Saverin Foundation has made an extraordinary $20 million grant to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute to accelerate research and care for people living with stage IV breast cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Susan G. Komen funds research into new breast cancer treatments
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In its mission to eradicate breast cancer, Susan G. Komen has invested nearly $1.1 billion in research since its founding in 1982. In 2023, Komen continued a longstanding partnership with Dana-Farber by awarding $2.3 million in new grants to Dana-Farber faculty members.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute Presidential Symposium
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In October, Dana-Farber supporters and leaders gathered for the annual Dana-Farber Cancer Institute Presidential Symposium. Attendees received firsthand updates on the State of the Institute, advances and opportunities in prevention and early detection, the impact of philanthropy on advancing research, and Dana-Farber’s world-renowned hematology/oncology fellowship program. jetpack-related-posts.title: AstraZeneca
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: AstraZeneca awarded over $360,000 to Dana-Farber to appoint a patient navigator to expand equitable access to clinical trials within the Breast Oncology Research Program. This navigator will proactively engage with patients with breast cancer and will focus on outreach and education to patients from historically marginalized communities to help navigate…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Transformational gift expands international fellowships in breast oncology
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Over the past 13 years, the Goldfarb and Rudkin Family International Fellowships in Breast Oncology at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute have accelerated scientific breakthroughs, fostered career growth through mentorship and collaboration, and advanced cancer care for patients around the world.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign: Closing the equity gap in cancer care
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Funds from The Dana-Farber Campaign allow us to expand access to underserved populations and improve research to reduce disparities in treatment outcomes.

content.rendered:
Spring 2025
By Samantha Sullivan

The National Foundation for Cancer Research awarded over $300,000 to Dana-Farber’s Kornelia Polyak, MD, PhD, to advance research in metastatic breast cancer. This funding will support her work in treatment resistance in HER2+ breast cancer brain metastases and ultimately make cures possible.

excerpt.rendered: The National Foundation for Cancer Research awarded over $300,000 to Dana-Farber’s Kornelia Polyak, MD, PhD, to advance research in metastatic breast cancer. This funding will support her work in treatment resistance in HER2+ breast cancer brain metastases and ultimately help transform the landscape of patient care.

jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Cancer Prevention Initiative (CPI) awarded $450,000 to Kornelia Polyak, MD, PhD, for her breast cancer research at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, targeting early tumor progression. This grant highlights CPI’s vital support for and shared mission with Dana-Farber in advancing impactful strategies for early medical interception of inherited cancer to improve…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Susan G. Komen funds research into new breast cancer treatments
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In its mission to eradicate breast cancer, Susan G. Komen has invested nearly $1.1 billion in research since its founding in 1982. In 2023, Komen continued a longstanding partnership with Dana-Farber by awarding $2.3 million in new grants to Dana-Farber faculty members.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Breast Cancer Research Foundation continues support with nearly $4 million in grants
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Since its founding by the late Evelyn Lauder alongside her dear friend Larry Norton, MD, in 1993, the Breast Cancer Research Foundation (BCRF) has championed research as the key to one day curing breast cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: American Cancer Society targets improved treatments and access
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Cancer Society (ACS) recently awarded $1.12 million in grants to four Dana-Farber researchers seeking to answer those questions and more.

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Legacy of Leadership and Hope: The Elaine and Eduardo Saverin Foundation’s generational commitment to patients with metastatic breast cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Elaine and Eduardo Saverin Foundation has made an extraordinary $20 million grant to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute to accelerate research and care for people living with stage IV breast cancer.

By Ross Perry

jetpack-related-posts.title: Estate of Carolyn Brophy
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Estate of Carolyn Brophy has generously bequeathed $120,697.36 to support cancer research and care at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. Carolyn’s commitment to Dana-Farber’s mission will drive promising research and innovative treatments. Her legacy will inspire breakthroughs and improve patient experiences, helping Dana-Farber continue to defy cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Impactful Progress: President and CEO Benjamin L. Ebert, MD, PhD, reflects on his first year and strategic vision for the future of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: As Dana-Farber Cancer Institute marks a transformative year under the leadership of President and CEO and Susan Smith Professor of Medicine at Harvard Medical School Benjamin L. Ebert, MD, PhD, Impact spoke with him about the significant milestones achieved and the exciting path ahead.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Society
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Dana-Farber Society (DFS) is a group of visionary donors who are changing lives and creating a legacy through a planned gift such as a bequest, life income gift, or beneficiary designation to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, the Jimmy Fund, the Friends of Dana-Farber, or the Pan-Mass Challenge.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Friends of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Friends of Dana-Farber hosted a variety of events throughout 2024 that raised more than $600,000 for lifesaving cancer research and patient care.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Giving Day celebrates 75 years of progress
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On May 22, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund held its fourth annual Giving Day—an inspirational day of hope, where supporters come together as a community to raise critical funds to defy cancer.

img.alt_text: A pediatric cancer patient smiling and holding a cookie

jetpack-related-posts.title: PopStroke
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: PopStroke completed its second annual October Breast Cancer Awareness Initiative, last year, in partnership with Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund. Throughout October, PopStroke locations nationally ran a number of initiatives to support breast cancer research and patient care at Dana-Farber, raising close to $145,000.

By Sofi Elbadawi

The Pediatric Cancer Research Foundation has awarded a $200,000 research grant to Brian Crompton, MD, for his work to test a prognostic liquid biopsy approach for pediatric Ewing sarcoma.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Children’s Cancer Research Fund
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Children’s Cancer Research Fund made two grants totaling $350,000 to support an early phase trial for relapsed pediatric liver cancer led by Allison O’Neill, MD, and liquid biopsy research in rhabdomyosarcoma led by Brian Crompton, MD. These pivotal resources help to develop more effective precision therapies for children facing…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Lee and Alexandria Zachos
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Lee and Alexandria Zachos made a gift of $100,000 to The Vasilios Kafkes Fund for Pediatric Cancer Research II at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, supporting Brian Crompton, MD, to advance ctDNA testing in pediatric tumors–a noninvasive blood test to improve detection, prevention, and care in childhood cancers–by developing a clinical assay…

jetpack-related-posts.title: St. Baldrick’s Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: St. Baldrick’s Foundation has awarded grants totaling $395,000 to fund pediatric cancer research by Institute researchers Rahela Aziz-Bose, MD, and Jun Qi, PhD. The grants will support their research to better understand and tackle barriers to nutrition for childhood cancer survivors and identify novel targets for pediatric brain tumors and…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Rally Foundation supports bold pediatric cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Rally Foundation for Childhood Cancer Research recently awarded $450,000 in grants to four Dana-Farber researchers developing innovative treatments for pediatric cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Children’s Cancer Research Fund
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Children’s Cancer Research Fund awarded their Emerging Scientist Award to Dana-Farber pediatric oncologist Emily Heikamp, MD, PhD, MSc. The grant of $100,000 will support Heikamp’s work in uncovering therapeutic vulnerabilities in the NU98-r gene, which could lead to safer and more effective treatments for children with relapsed acute myeloid leukemia.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Grants support innovations in pediatric cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For over 12 years, grants awarded by Hyundai Hope On Wheels® totaling over $5.5 million have supported Dana-Farber investigators and their research to further discovery, leverage new technologies, and revolutionize treatment for pediatric patients everywhere.

content.rendered:
Spring 2025
By Sofi Elbadawi

St. Baldrick’s Foundation has awarded grants totaling $395,000 to fund pediatric cancer research by Institute researchers Rahela Aziz-Bose, MD, and Jun Qi, PhD. The grants will support their research to better understand and tackle barriers to nutrition for childhood cancer survivors and identify novel targets for pediatric brain tumors and develop new strategies to suppress the targets for patient treatment, respectively.

jetpack-related-posts.title: St. Baldrick’s Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: St. Baldrick’s Foundation renewed their support for Dana-Farber with grants totaling nearly $200,000 to fund studies that will lay the groundwork for better precision medicine approaches for children with leukemia. These projects, led by Dana-Farber, involve collaboration with multiple institutions in the U.S. and abroad.

jetpack-related-posts.title: St. Baldrick’s Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: St. Baldrick’s Foundation awarded a total of $415,000 to Dana-Farber studies into how neuroblastoma, one of the most common pediatric solid tumors, escapes destruction by the immune system; and how a category of newly discovered “dark proteins” may point toward new approaches to treat medulloblastoma, a devastating form of childhood…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Grants support innovations in pediatric cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For over 12 years, grants awarded by Hyundai Hope On Wheels® totaling over $5.5 million have supported Dana-Farber investigators and their research to further discovery, leverage new technologies, and revolutionize treatment for pediatric patients everywhere.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Conquer Cancer fuels five groundbreaking studies
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Conquer Cancer®, the ASCO Foundation, is accelerating discovery Institute-wide, from pediatrics to rare sarcomas.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Rallying to defy pediatric cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Bolstering Dana-Farber’s mission to defy cancer, Rally Foundation for Childhood Cancer Research made grants totaling $850,000 in 2023 to help drive much-needed progress in pediatric oncology research.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Conquer Cancer® grants target several types of cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Conquer Cancer®, the ASCO Foundation, has fueled groundbreaking research at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute for decades.

content.rendered:
Spring 2025
By Kayla McMahon

Swim Across America raised $250,000 in 2024 to benefit Dana-Farber’s Perini Family Survivors’ Center. Since 1996, the Boston Open Water Swim has united swimmers of all ages and abilities, raising over $3.5 million in total to support vital survivorship research at Dana-Farber and continuing to “Make Waves Against Cancer.”

jetpack-related-posts.title: Swim Across America
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Swim Across America’s Boston Open Water Swim raised $335,000 in 2025 to benefit patients who receive care at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and their families. Raising over $3.8 million since 1996, the organization continues to “Make Waves to Fight Cancer” and fuel critical survivorship research at Dana-Farber. This year's event will…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Swim Across America
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For 27 years, Swim Across America has supported Dana-Farber through events like their annual Boston Open Water Swim event. In 2022, swimmers of all ages and skill levels raised $142,000 to help support cancer research and care at the Institute, for a lifetime total of more than $3 million.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Swim Across America
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Swim Across America hosted their 28th annual Boston Open Water Swim event, which directly benefits Dana-Farber patients and families. Swimmers of all ages and skills levels united to “Make Waves Against Cancer” and raised $175,000, bringing the event’s cumulative fundraising total to over $3 million to date.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Ravestock Boston
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Ravestock Boston, hosted in October by the William Raveis Charitable Fund, raised nearly $150,000 for Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s life-changing mission. Held in memory of Meghan Raveis, the event brought together community and live music to benefit Dana-Farber's cancer research and care, while honoring Meghan’s legacy of service to others.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Cross-Check Cancer Women’s Hockey Tournament
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The annual Cross-Check Cancer Women’s Hockey Tournament raised more than $40,000 in 2022, a new record, to support the Adult Survivorship Program in the Perini Family Survivors’ Center at Dana-Farber. The tournament draws 38 teams and more than 470 participants from 11 states to raise funds to ensure a healthy…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Friends of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Friends of Dana-Farber hosted a variety of events throughout 2024 that raised more than $600,000 for lifesaving cancer research and patient care.

By Casey Repasy

jetpack-related-posts.title: Expanding equitable access to critical care
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Last year, the National Breast Cancer Foundation (NBCF) generously provided $155,000 to support Dana-Farber’s inclusion, diversity, and equity work to ensure equitable health outcomes for all.

img.alt_text: National Breast Cancer Foundation, Inc. Logo

jetpack-related-posts.title: National Foundation for Cancer Research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The National Foundation for Cancer Research awarded over $300,000 to Dana-Farber’s Kornelia Polyak, MD, PhD, to advance research in metastatic breast cancer. This funding will support her work in treatment resistance in HER2+ breast cancer brain metastases and ultimately help transform the landscape of patient care.

img.alt_text: National Foundation for Cancer Research logo

jetpack-related-posts.title: Gabrielle’s Angel Foundation for Cancer Research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Gabrielle’s Angel Foundation for Cancer Research awarded $250,000 to Dana-Farber’s Zuzana Tothova, MD, PhD, who is exploring the biology of cohesin mutations, frequent and recurrent drivers of myelodysplastic syndromes and acute myeloid leukemia. With this funding, Tothova aims to develop targeted treatments for these cancers.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Massachusetts Life Sciences Center fuels advances in immunotherapy and workforce development
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute has received nearly $800,000 in support from the Massachusetts Life Sciences Center (MLSC) to advance cancer research and workforce development.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Melanoma Research Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Melanoma Research Foundation has awarded Dana-Farber’s Pere Puigserver, PhD, with a prestigious $200,000 Established Investigator Award. Puigserver’s pioneering research aims to revolutionize immunotherapeutic approaches for metastatic melanoma, with a focus on overcoming drug resistance and improving patient survival outcomes.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Louis B. Mayer Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Louis B. Mayer Foundation awarded grants totaling $100,000 to support Dana-Farber’s efforts in developing personalized vaccines to treat chronic lymphocytic leukemia; deepening our understanding of neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) to inform better treatment options; and developing personalized treatments for patients at high risk for HER2-positive breast cancer.

content.rendered:
Spring 2025

Dear Friends,

At its root, “defy” means to challenge or to do something considered impossible. The Dana-Farber Campaign—our historic, $2.5 billion fundraising effort that wrapped up at the end of September 2024—unequivocally pushed the boundaries of what is possible for the Institute and our patients.

More than 900,000 donors from here and abroad contributed 2.3 million gifts to this historic effort—more than 63% of which were received from first-time donors. The impact of the campaign has touched every part of Dana-Farber’s work and mission. We saw the establishment of 49 new endowed positions for our faculty and fellows, the launch of many new centers and programs, and key advances in initiatives across immunotherapy and vaccine development, artificial intelligence, drug discovery, cancer care equity, pediatric research and care, and more.

None of this would have been possible without our vast community of supporters, scientists, clinical staff, and friends, as well as the incredible leadership of Laurie H. Glimcher, MD, president emerita of Dana-Farber, who launched The Dana-Farber Campaign in 2017 to advance her strategic vision for the Institute. In many ways, it is fitting that her tenure as president and CEO ended as we closed the books on this historic campaign—one that has changed the world of cancer research and treatment.

On behalf of our entire team, past and present, I can confidently say that we have been the beneficiaries of the true partnership and the love of humankind that is at the center of philanthropy. Because of you, this campaign, and your leadership, our impact and growth will expand by an order of magnitude we have only begun to imagine. I am so excited to see what heights we reach next, together.

Melany N. Duval
Senior Vice President and Chief Philanthropy Officer

excerpt.rendered: Because of your support for The Dana-Farber Campaign, our impact and growth will expand by an order of magnitude we have only begun to imagine.

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Message from Melany Duval
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Over the past seven years, The Dana-Farber Campaign has enabled incredible progress at the Institute, the effects of which ripple out to help patients around the world.

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Message from Melany Duval
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: When I first stepped into my role at Dana-Farber in 2019, I was immediately struck by the endless compassion and dedication of the people around me.

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Message from Melany Duval
jetpack-related-posts.author: danafarberandthejimmyfund@gmail.com
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: We are thrilled to unveil the Spring 2023 issue of Impact—the first of our newly redesigned magazine and website!

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Message from Melany Duval
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: September has arrived, and with it the end of summer and the close of another successful Jimmy Fund event season.

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Message from Melany Duval
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Thanks to the tenacity and generosity of our entire community over the last seven years of The Dana-Farber Campaign, we are defying cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Message from Melany Duval
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: One of the things that makes Dana-Farber such a special place is our emphasis on teamwork.

content.rendered:
Spring 2025
By Kathy Clute

Together, we are defying cancer

Because you believe in us, support us, and invest in us, together we have made stunning leaps forward in diagnosing, treating, and understanding cancer.

The Dana-Farber Campaign came to a successful close on Sept. 30, 2024, after nearly a million people in all 50 states and 117 countries donated a record-breaking $2.5 billion to defy cancer. Your remarkable generosity has funded paradigm-shifting research, novel treatments, new world-class facilities, additional clinical trials, and many ambitious initiatives that lessen the burden of cancer for patients and their families here and around the globe.

The seven-year Dana-Farber Campaign was one of the largest fundraising efforts ever in the U.S. devoted entirely to cancer, and it reflected the vision and strategic priorities of President Emerita Laurie H. Glimcher, MD, who stepped down as president and CEO last fall. “Dr. Glimcher’s emphasis on priorities to transform the cancer care and research landscape were foundational to the campaign,” said Institute Trustee and Campaign Chair Michael Eisenson, who led the campaign in partnership with Trustee and Campaign Vice Chair Monica Chandra. “And it will shape Dana-Farber and the field of oncology for decades to come.”

The campaign inspired more than 2.3 million gifts from 928,000 donors, including 1.5 million gifts of under $100 from Jimmy Fund supporters and fundraisers. The largest single contributor to the campaign was the Pan-Mass Challenge, giving $425 million raised via 2.2 million gifts since 2017.

The Dana-Farber Campaign by the numbers:

2.3 million gifts
928,000+ donors
1.5 million gifts under $100
100% participation by the Board of Trustees
100% participation by senior faculty and staff
18 new centers and programs
49 endowed positions
3 new patient care facilities
32.5% increase in clinical trials

Highlights of The Dana-Farber Campaign

Our research led to FDA approval of the first epigenetic drug to treat solid tumors, which will aid in the development of other epigenetic drugs.

We are caring for more people with cancer. Patient volume has grown by 51% since 2017.

Clinical trials have grown by 32.5 %, with more than 1,100 active trials underway today.

The Cancer Care Equity Program more than doubled in size, allowing support for more patients from historically marginalized and medically underserved communities.

We opened three new world-class patient care facilities in Massachusetts—in the Merrimack Valley, Chestnut Hill, and Foxborough—that allow patients to receive the best in cancer care closer to home.

We launched the Centers for Early Detection and Interception, a first-of-its-kind integrated clinic to detect precancerous conditions early and to prevent cancer from developing in individuals at higher risk for the disease.

We earned our fifth consecutive Magnet® designation from the American Nurses Credentialing Center, a recognition of our high-quality care and our commitment to nursing excellence. Fewer than 1% of the nation’s hospitals have achieved Magnet status five times in a row.

We developed an artificial intelligence tool that can determine from routine radiology reports whether lung cancer is present and if it is responding to treatment, which could facilitate delivery of precision medicine at scale.

To learn more about all our progress thanks to your support, visit DefyCancer.org.

jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Campaign Cabinet devoted their time, talents, and resources to advancing The Dana-Farber Campaign’s mission to Defy Cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Data science and AI allow us to better match patients to clinical trials, identify disparities in cancer care, and pinpoint the most promising treatment options.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign: The promise of personalized cancer vaccines
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Funds raised through The Dana-Farber campaign are expanding the benefits of personalized cancer vaccines pioneered here.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign: FDA approves new pediatric brain cancer drug
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Support for The Dana-Farber Campaign advanced research leading to approval of the new treatment for pediatric low-grade glioma (PLGA).

img.alt_text: A doctor smiles and listens to the heartbeat of a young patient

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On Sept. 30, Dana-Farber announced the completion of one of the largest-ever fundraising campaigns focused solely on cancer: The Dana-Farber Campaign.

jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Defy Cancer Celebration at Fenway Park on Sunday, March 30, was a day filled with hope, progress, and community. It highlighted the impact and innovation in cancer care and research made possible by gifts to The Dana-Farber Campaign from 2017 to 2024.

title.rendered: One in a billion: Pan-Mass Challenge surpasses $1 billion fundraising milestone

content.rendered:
Winter 2024
By Michael Quinn
Photography by Pan-Mass Challenge

For more than four and a half decades, the Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC), a bike-a-thon across Massachusetts and the world’s most successful single athletic fundraising event, has been an integral partner in Dana-Farber’s life-changing work. Even by the PMC’s lofty standards, 2024 was a banner year, as the organization generated a record gift of $75 million and surpassed an extraordinary $1.047 billion in lifetime fundraising since its founding in 1980.

This historic effort was accelerated by the 45th PMC ride on August 3–4, when more than 6,800 riders from 45 states and territories and 10 countries pedaled 16 one- and two-day routes ranging from 25 to 211 miles across Massachusetts. They were supported by over 3,500 volunteers, more than 200 corporate sponsors, and 350,000 individual donations. More than 1,100 riders and volunteers were cancer patients and survivors, considered Living Proof of the PMC’s mission and impact. PMC fundraising was also propelled by PMC Winter Cycle, an annual spin event at Fenway Park in Boston; PMC Unpaved, a gravel ride in the Berkshires in Western Massachusetts; and PMC Kids Rides, where children raise funds through mini bike-a-thons in their communities.

The PMC donates 100% of every rider-raised dollar to Dana-Farber. As the Institute’s largest single donor, accounting for 66% of the Jimmy Fund’s annual revenue, the PMC remains the driving force for progress at the Institute that ripples around the globe. And the advances at Dana-Farber enabled by the PMC since its inception have transformed cancer medicine.

For example, immunotherapy, the gold standard for treating many cancers today, arose from innovative basic research discoveries made at the Institute that relied on PMC support. Since then, Dana-Farber researchers unleashed these breakthrough treatments against malignancies like melanoma, for which the Institute’s team led the first trials of immunotherapies and cancer vaccines.

PMC funding also fueled the growth of Dana-Farber’s clinical trials program into one of the nation’s largest, allowing the Institute to play a substantial role in advancing more than half of all cancer therapies approved by the FDA in the last five years. In multiple myeloma, many of the 19 therapies approved in the past two decades were advanced at the Institute with PMC support, with patients now living three to five times longer than could be previously expected.

Additionally, funding from the PMC has helped the Institute more than double in size since 2000, from approximately 1.22 million square feet then to more than 2.83 million square feet in 2024. This new space includes three world-class patient care facilities built in the past five years to bring cancer care into communities closer to where patients live; and dynamic research labs like the Longwood Center, the Institute’s state-of-the art hub of collaborative, leading-edge cancer science.

Along with its physical footprint, Dana-Farber expanded care for historically marginalized populations as the Cancer Care Equity Program doubled in size, enabling the Institute to increase its team of community-facing patient navigators, build relationships with neighborhood clinics, and expand research into the causes of and interventions for health disparities.

In parallel, PMC resources equipped Dana-Farber to recruit and retain renowned physicians, scientists, and nurses from around the globe, with more than 125 physicians named to Boston magazine’s most recent “Top Doctors” list, 34 investigators on the “Highly Cited Researchers” list by the Institute for Scientific Information at Clarivate, and the fifth consecutive Magnet® designation for excellence in nursing and patient care.

Bolder research, better care, optimal facilities, and the best people—these things and more are what $1 billion from the PMC has made possible at Dana-Farber. This tremendous progress helped the number of cancer survivors in the U.S. grow from less than 5 million in 1980 to over 19 million in 2024, and the five-year survival rate increase from 50% to 68%.

For Benjamin Ebert, MD, PhD, Dana-Farber president and CEO, the George P. Canellos, MD, and Jean S. Canellos Professor of Medicine, and 6-year PMC rider, the PMC is much more than a bike ride—it is a lifeline for the Institute’s mission to defy cancer. “The PMC is an experience like none other,” Ebert said. “I am honored to ride each summer with this committed community, which inspires us all at Dana-Farber and empowers everything we do to improve patients’ lives.”

In celebrating a year that was truly “One In a Billion,” Billy Starr—PMC founder and executive director, 45-year PMC rider, and a Dana-Farber Trustee—knows this dedicated community is ready for more. “I am immensely grateful to everyone who has contributed to this $1 billion fundraising achievement,” Starr said. “Together, we’re setting up the road to the next billion and even greater progress.”

jetpack-related-posts.title: Wheeling in the years: The Pan-Mass Challenge produces origin story video
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In 2024, to mark its 45th ride and to celebrate crossing a phenomenal $1 billion in lifetime fundraising, the PMC created a film bringing its origin story to life.

jetpack-related-posts.title: PMC Winter Cycle
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The one-of-a-kind PMC Winter Cycle was held at Fenway Park on March 9, with hundreds of riders participating to support patient care and research at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute.

img.alt_text: Cyclists participating in the PMC Winter Cycle at Fenway Park

jetpack-related-posts.title: Pan-Mass Challenge raises record $72 million to bring cures closer by the mile
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On long journeys, landmarks and milestones show us where we are and how far we’ve come. Since 1980, the Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC), the beloved bike-a-thon and the nation’s most successful athletic fundraiser, has seen plenty of both.

img.alt_text: Pan-Mass Challenge riders along the route

jetpack-related-posts.title: 2025 PMC Winter Cycle
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC), the nation’s single most successful athletic fundraiser and Dana-Farber’s largest single contributor, kicked off its 2025 fundraising year at the 10th PMC Winter Cycle on Feb. 1 at Fenway Park.

img.alt_text: Bikers on stationary bikes at the PMC Winter Cycle event

jetpack-related-posts.title: Pan-Mass Challenge is moving to Worcester
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC), which has raised $1.125 billion for Dana-Farber Cancer Institute since 1980, is relocating its starting line and hub site from Sturbridge to Worcester.

jetpack-related-posts.title: PMC Winter Cycle
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On Feb. 4, hundreds of riders assembled at Fenway Park’s 521 Overlook venue for the PMC Winter Cycle.

img.alt_text: Cyclists on stationary bikes at the 2023 PMC Winter Cycle

title.rendered: A new chapter in Dana-Farber leadership

content.rendered:
Winter 2024
By Ellen Berlin
Photography by John Deputy

Laurie H. Glimcher, MD, an esteemed health care executive and renowned immuno-oncologist, stepped down as Dana-Farber Cancer Institute President and CEO on October 1 and assumed the title of President Emerita. Glimcher will continue both her pioneering research and her mentorship of the next generation of physician-scientists at Dana-Farber, along with other special projects.

Since becoming the seventh president of Dana-Farber in October 2016—and the first woman to lead the organization in its 77-year history—Glimcher has maintained a relentless focus on improving outcomes for patients and accelerating cancer drug development. Under Glimcher’s leadership, Dana-Farber is credited for playing a critical role in the development of 51% of all cancer drugs approved by the FDA over the past five years. The Institute expanded regional locations from four to seven, and saw dramatic growth in patient volume and in grant and industry-funded research support. Glimcher spearheaded Dana-Farber’s proposal to build a new 300-bed inpatient hospital dedicated to adult patients with cancer and a new collaboration with Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, and expanded the Institute’s Cancer Care Equity Program, which is at the forefront of efforts to reduce disparities in cancer outcomes for historically marginalized groups.

“Eight years ago, I began this journey with a deep appreciation for the extraordinary research that emanated from Dana-Farber since its earliest days and the clinical excellence that Dana-Farber provides patients and families,” said Glimcher. “And now, as I reflect on my tenure, I am intensely proud of what we have achieved in providing world-class care for our patients, leading in innovation, and discovering new treatments and cures.”

Glimcher led The Dana-Farber Campaign, the most ambitious fundraising effort in the history of the Institute and one of the largest in the U.S. focused solely on cancer. The Dana-Farber Campaign closed at the end of September far above its original goal and has accelerated the Institute’s strategic priorities supporting revolutionary science and extraordinary care.

“This is the perfect time for me to pass the leadership of this remarkable institution on to the next generation, and return my focus to cancer immunology research,” Glimcher said.

“Laurie Glimcher’s tenure as Dana-Farber’s president has been transformative and impactful for our patients, our physician-scientists, our workforce, and the entire oncology community,” said Josh Bekenstein, Dana-Farber Board Chair. “Dana-Farber has been extremely fortunate to have had a President and CEO of Laurie Glimcher’s scientific stature who has also proven to be a visionary, compassionate, and inclusive leader. Her patient-centered approach helped the Institute continue to improve the great care at Dana-Farber. I am incredibly grateful for her brilliant leadership.”

Benjamin L. Ebert, MD, PhD, a world-renowned medical oncologist and researcher who most recently served as chair of Dana-Farber’s Department of Medical Oncology, was named by the Board of Trustees to succeed Glimcher effective October 1.

“With a very strong foundation built on Laurie’s extremely accomplished and successful tenure and now with Ben’s leadership, Dana-Farber will continue being a world leader in cancer care and research.”

Josh Bekenstein, Chairman, Dana-Farber Board of Trustees

“Ben has been a tremendously effective leader of our Department of Medical Oncology. As we plan for the future of cancer care and discovery, we are confident that he will take on the new challenge as he has all others—with integrity, thoughtfulness, diligence, and compassion,” said Bekenstein. “His leadership and experience will be extremely beneficial as we plan for the proposed new cancer hospital and clinical collaboration.”

As head of Medical Oncology, Ebert oversaw a period of dramatic growth in the number of faculty, clinical volume, and research funding. His initiatives include programs for early career faculty mentorship, faculty well-being, and increased multi-disciplinary collaboration. He leads a research laboratory that focuses on the molecular basis and treatment of hematologic malignancies and their nonmalignant precursor conditions, with a particular focus on myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS) and clonal hematopoiesis.

“I’m extraordinarily honored to be selected as the next president and CEO of Dana-Farber and to build on the exceptional leadership and accomplishments of Laurie Glimcher,” said Ebert. “Dana-Farber is truly a remarkable organization and a global leader in innovation, and in caring and advocating for cancer patients. Together with our executive leadership team, I will continue to advance a patient-first model as we open this new chapter.”

Ebert is an elected member of the National Academy of Medicine, the American Academy of Arts and Sciences, the American Society for Clinical Investigation, the Association of American Physicians, and the Academy of the American Association for Cancer Research, and has won numerous prestigious national and international awards.

“With a very strong foundation built on Laurie’s extremely accomplished and successful tenure and now with Ben’s leadership, Dana-Farber will continue being a world leader in cancer care and research,” said Bekenstein.

title.rendered: Krafts champion early detection and prevention for at-risk communities

content.rendered:
Winter 2024
By Caitlin Henault
Photography by Michael Blanchard

For more than 50 years, the Kraft family and Dana-Farber have shared a visionary partnership in support of a common mission: to make a difference in the lives of patients in New England and beyond. With a gift of $5 million to The Dana-Farber Campaign, the family will bring Dana-Farber’s lifesaving early detection and prevention programs to more people at risk of developing cancer.

The Kraft family is funding a program to support health equity efforts in Dana-Farber’s Centers for Early Detection and Interception (CEDI). Launched in 2023, CEDI is a first-of-its-kind, integrated clinical and research program that develops novel technologies and methods for cancer detection and prevention. The Kraft’s gift will advance work led by Sapna Syngal, MD, MPH, to support dedicated staff focused on expanding access to early detection screenings and education for at-risk populations throughout Dana-Farber’s existing network of community-based health clinics. A portion of the gift previously established the Kraft Family Chair, held by Nikhil Munshi, MD.

“Despite enormous progress in early detection and prevention over the past several decades, historically marginalized populations still bear a disproportionate cancer burden,” said Syngal, who serves as co-director of CEDI. “This program brings CEDI’s lifesaving resources to more people in our communities and has the potential to serve as a national model for addressing disparities in cancer care.”

Syngal will collaborate with Magnolia Contreras, MSW, MBA, vice president of Community Health, and Christopher Lathan, MD, MS, MPH, chief clinical access officer and the Hadley Family Chair at Dana-Farber, to identify individuals in local communities at risk of developing cancer, implement screenings, and facilitate enrollment in clinical trials.

The Kraft family has played a pivotal role in many landmark initiatives at Dana-Farber, including the creation of the Cancer Care Equity Program, led by Lathan; the establishment of the Kraft Family Blood Donor Center at Dana-Farber and Brigham and Women’s Hospital; the endowment of the Kraft Family Professorship held by Kenneth Anderson, MD; and support for ovarian cancer and multiple myeloma research in memory of Myra Kraft and New England Patriots player Ron Burton. Robert Kraft served as a Dana-Farber Trustee for nearly 45 years, and Dan Kraft joined the board in 2012.

“The Kraft family continues to demonstrate a generous and heartfelt commitment to our community by connecting at-risk populations to resources and programs that will save their lives,” said Laurie H. Glimcher, MD, president emerita of Dana-Farber and the Richard and Susan Smith Professor of Medicine. “They are further elevating our unrelenting efforts to ensure that everyone benefits from world-class cancer care, no matter their zip code or socio-economic status.”

“By expanding access to early detection and prevention resources, we hope to reduce the burden of cancer treatment for patients and families down the road,” said Dan Kraft. “Dana-Farber has the vision and the track record to level the playing field, and we believe this program will make a real difference in saving lives.”

excerpt.rendered: With a gift of $5 million to The Dana-Farber Campaign, the Kraft Family will bring Dana-Farber’s lifesaving early detection and prevention programs to more people at risk of developing cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Stopping cancer before it starts
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: When The Dana-Farber Campaign was announced in 2021, cancer early detection and interception represented a key priority to re-imagine cancer care and it remains so today.

img.alt_text: Steaming beaker and pipette in the lab

jetpack-related-posts.title: Paving the way to cancer prevention
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Wycliffe “Wyc” Grousbeck and Emilia Fazzalari are firm believers that “good things don’t come easy.” As philanthropic and entrepreneurial leaders in the Boston community, they seek out innovative and exceptional people who are tackling groundbreaking endeavors that are simply too compelling to refuse.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jeannie and Jonathan Lavine Endowed Chairs for Preventive Cancer Therapies
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In 2020, Jeannie and Jonathan Lavine endowed three Dana-Farber Chairs in support of prevention and early detection research at the Institute, with a gift to The Dana-Farber Campaign.

img.alt_text: Catherine Wu, MD; Laurie H. Glimcher, MD; and Jonathan Lavine

jetpack-related-posts.title: Stanley and Carol Riemer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Carol and Stanley Riemer’s most recent commitment has established the Riemer Family Fund for Pancreatic Cancer Early Detection at Dana-Farber, in honor of late relatives who developed pancreatic cancer. Under the leadership of Matthew Yurgelun, MD, their support aims to develop groundbreaking early detection blood tests for high-risk patients.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Priscilla Lawrence and Patrick MeLampy
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A new $1 million gift from Rev. Dr. Priscilla Lawrence and Patrick MeLampy will advance the work of Irene Ghobrial, MD, a Lavine Family Chair for Preventative Cancer Therapies at Dana-Farber, and the Center for Early Detection and Interception of Blood Cancers to better understand risk factors for multiple myeloma…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Cancer Prevention Initiative
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Cancer Prevention Initiative (CPI) awarded $450,000 to Kornelia Polyak, MD, PhD, for her breast cancer research at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, targeting early tumor progression. This grant highlights CPI’s vital support for and shared mission with Dana-Farber in advancing impactful strategies for early medical interception of inherited cancer to improve…

title.rendered: Another home run year for the Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon

content.rendered:
Winter 2024
By Nathalie Sczublewski, Robbie Merritt
Photography by John Deputy

The WEEI/NESN Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon presented by Arbella Insurance helped strike out cancer for the 22nd year at Fenway Park in August, with the help of thousands of generous supporters from across the country. The two-day event, which features inspiring stories from patients and doctors at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, community leaders, and other special guests, raised nearly $4 million for adult and pediatric cancer care and research at Dana-Farber.

Broadcast live from Fenway Park Aug. 13 and 14 from 6 a.m. through midnight, the fundraiser featured Dana-Farber pediatric and adult patients who shared their stories on-air and took part in special on-field ceremonies. Threaded throughout the event were moving tributes to two Boston Red Sox and Jimmy Fund heroes who passed away over the past year: Chairman of the Jimmy Fund and Institute Trustee Larry Lucchino, and the first-ever Jimmy Fund Co-Captain Tim Wakefield.

Kicking off the fundraising each morning was a special matching challenge from Rob and Karen Hale, who pledged to match the first $775,000 raised between 6 and 10 a.m. over the two days. Other special appearances included new Jimmy Fund Co-Chairs Brock Holt and Tom Caron; Jimmy Fund Captain and Red Sox pitcher Garrett Whitlock; Red Sox Manager Alex Cora; Boston Bruins goaltender Jeremy Swayman; New England Revolution head coach Caleb Porter, and many others.

“We feel extremely lucky to join the team every year at Radio-Telethon,” said Gayle O’Connell, executive vice president and CMO of the Arbella Insurance Group. “I think we all know someone who is fighting a battle with cancer, so supporting the important work that the heroes at Dana-Farber do each day is an honor for us.”

“At a time when life is more expensive than ever, our listeners, clients, and partners stepped up and gave once again!” said Mike Thomas, senior vice president and market manager of Audacy Boston, parent company of WEEI. “The athletes and celebrities who took the time to come on and help us raise money are inspiring.”

“The overwhelming generosity of our viewers and partners demonstrates the deep commitment that the audience has to fighting cancer,” said Sean McGrail, president & CEO of NESN. “Together, we will continue to make a significant impact in the lives of patients and their families.”

jetpack-related-posts.title: WEEI/NESN Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon surpasses $70 million
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Thanks to thousands of generous supporters from across the country, the 21st annual WEEI/NESN Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon presented by Arbella Insurance raised more than $4 million.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Arbella Insurance Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Arbella Insurance Foundation continued its steadfast support of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute through its Strike Out Cancer Program. At the 2025 WEEI/NESN Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon, the team presented a check for $100,000, part of the more than $1.7 million the Arbella Insurance Foundation has contributed to date.

img.alt_text: Arbella Insurance Foundation employees with a check at the Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon breaks records with $5.7 million raised for Dana-Farber
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The WEEI/NESN Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon presented by Arbella Insurance continued to be a beacon of support for Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund in August with a record-breaking fundraising year.

jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Since 1953, the Boston Red Sox have had a deep and multifaceted impact on patients with cancer through its strong partnership with Dana-Farber and the Jimmy Fund.

img.alt_text: Dana-Farber patient and doctor on the field at Fenway Park

jetpack-related-posts.title: Michael and Christina Gordon
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Trustee Michael Gordon and his wife, Christina, continue to invest in Dana-Farber’s commitment to transformative cancer care. Through a generous gift of $212,000 the Gordons are graciously supporting the Howard G. Gordon Family Teen Activities Fund, the WEEI/NESN Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon, the Trustee Annual Fund, and the Laurie H. Glimcher,…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Arbella Insurance Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Celebrating its 10th anniversary, the Arbella Insurance Foundation continued its Strike Out Cancer program, where $50 per Red Sox strikeout, up to $100,000, is donated each season. With their $100,000 contribution in 2024, the foundation surpassed $1.2 million raised to date, underscoring Arbella Insurance’s vital partnership in defying cancer.

title.rendered: American Cancer Society enables pathbreaking new inquiries

content.rendered:
Winter 2024
By Kathy Clute
Photography by Sam Ogden and Sasha Pedro

The American Cancer Society built upon more than 75 years of support for Dana-Farber by recently awarding nearly $3.1 million in new grants to 11 investigators across the Institute. The awards will fund a broad spectrum of research ranging from basic science inquiries to psychosocial interventions for patients and survivors.

Kira Bona, MD, MPH, is using her Discovery Boost Grant to test the feasibility of a random pilot intervention of cash transfers to low-income families whose children have been recently diagnosed with cancer. Studies show that these children are more likely to relapse and die, even when they receive the same chemotherapy as their peers in higher-income families.

A TheoryLab Collaborative Grant is funding research led by Abby Rosenberg, MD, MS, MA, chief of Pediatric Palliative Care, into whether an online coaching and stress-management tool can alleviate distress in breast cancer survivors who fear that their disease will recur. “These patients are particularly vulnerable to psychological distress—especially if they are single parents, have financial difficulties, or live in under-resourced communities,” said Rosenberg.

Jennifer Snaman, MD, received a Clinician Scientist Development Grant to test whether a decision-making tool developed for adolescent and young adult (AYA) patients could be modified for use by younger teens.

AYA patients often have views different from their parents about what kind of treatment they wish to have, especially near end of life, Snaman said. She is interviewing AYAs and their parents to learn more about their approach to treatment decision-making and using this information to adapt an online tool known as MyPref. Her goal is to improve patient, family, and physician communication and decision-making.

The American Cancer Society also awarded postdoctoral fellowships to Ke Cong, PhD, and Cheuk-Ting Law, PhD. Cong is investigating the role of the protein CDK5 in DNA replication stress, a condition linked to genomic instability and cancer development. Law is developing an innovative sequencing technology to delve into the LINE-1 gene, which has recently been recognized for its role in causing large-scale mutagenesis in cancer and its cancer biomarker potential. These projects are expected to provide insights into possible new cancer therapies.

Other recent awardees are Pratiti Bandopadhayay, MBBS, PhD; Christina Dieli-Conwright, PhD, MPH; Jennifer Karlow, PhD; Christopher Lathan, MD, MS, MPH, chief clinical access and equity officer and the Hadley Family Chair at Dana-Farber; Christopher Manz, MD; and Baochun Zhang, MD, PhD.

“Our research goal is to find answers that help save lives, and that means funding the most innovative cancer research,” said William Dahut, MD, chief scientific officer at the American Cancer Society. “These grantees represent the very best to help break new ground in cancer care and treatment.”

excerpt.rendered: Recent grants from the American Cancer Society fund innovative projects across Dana-Farber, from basic science to pediatric cancer disparities.

jetpack-related-posts.title: American Cancer Society grants propel research and programs forward
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Cancer Society (ACS) recently awarded more than $3.1 million in grants to 11 Dana-Farber Cancer Institute investigators. These grants support various areas across Dana-Farber, including research on improved outcomes and patient assistance programming to help with access to care.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber researchers awarded American Society of Hematology funding
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Society of Hematology (ASH) funds groundbreaking research on blood and bone marrow disorders. Over the past year, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute researchers have earned a total of $845,000 in competitive ASH grants.

jetpack-related-posts.title: American Cancer Society targets improved treatments and access
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Cancer Society (ACS) recently awarded $1.12 million in grants to four Dana-Farber researchers seeking to answer those questions and more.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Human Frontier Science Program
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Human Frontier Science Program, an organization that promotes international collaboration in basic research, awarded grants totaling more than $400,000 to fund biochemistry research at Dana-Farber. The funding supports two early career researchers pursuing projects that seek to deepen our understanding of the tumor microenvironment and develop cutting-edge strategies to…

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Society
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Dana-Farber Society (DFS) is a group of visionary donors who are changing lives and creating a legacy through a planned gift such as a bequest, life income gift, or beneficiary designation to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, the Jimmy Fund, the Friends of Dana-Farber, or the Pan-Mass Challenge.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Prostate Cancer Foundation fuels Dana-Farber innovation with $1M+ in grants
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: PCF recently awarded $1,050,000 to three Dana-Farber Cancer Institute researchers through two Young Investigator Awards and one Challenge Award, each supporting research projects aimed at combating prostate cancer and improving outcomes for patients.

content.rendered:
Winter 2024
By Casey Reis

Last summer, HomeGoods and Homesense customers found more than an ever-changing assortment of exciting merchandise at store locations across the nation. From May 30 through June 26, the off-price retailers teamed up with Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund in its 24th annual campaign to help families facing cancer, raising critical funding for revolutionary cancer research and compassionate patient care.

The “Find Home Anywhere” initiative invited shoppers in more than 900 HomeGoods and Homesense locations nationwide to make a donation at the register, with 100% of donations benefiting Dana-Farber and the Jimmy Fund. Customers were also able to purchase two limited-edition reusable shopping bags at $0.99 each, featuring artwork by 7-year-old Emelie of Natick, Mass. (pictured), a patient in Dana-Farber’s Jimmy Fund Clinic. A portion of the sale from each bag purchased went directly to the Jimmy Fund.

In August 2022, Emelie began experiencing severe stomach pain and a bump was discovered on her right side. When testing revealed that Emelie had bilateral Wilms tumor—a form of kidney cancer—her family headed to Dana-Farber for treatment. Since her diagnosis, Emelie has undergone a combination of surgery, chemotherapy, and post-chemo medications to combat the disease.

At Dana-Farber’s Jimmy Fund Clinic, the team welcomed and supported Emelie, providing a home away from home when she needed it most. Emelie had taken a special interest in painting and crafting at the Clinic, and was thrilled when her colorful, whimsical artwork—one design featuring a panda munching on watermelon, and another showcasing sea life swimming in turquoise blue water—was selected for the 2024 HomeGoods bag designs. Emelie was excited to visit a HomeGoods location over the summer and see the bags on display, knowing that her artwork is helping to fuel advancements in cancer treatment for patients like herself. In addition to arts and crafts, Emelie also loves basketball, gymnastics, and being a Girl Scout.

HomeGoods has been a steadfast partner in Dana-Farber’s lifesaving mission since 2001, raising more than $30 million through the generosity of its customers to prevent, treat, and defy cancer. “HomeGoods and Dana-Farber have long shared an interest in creating a sense of home, safety, comfort, and belonging for patients,” said Victoria Shonkoff, senior vice president and marketing director, HomeGoods and Homesense. “Together with our generous customers, we’re proud to support patients like Emelie and help provide a sense of comfort for them and their families throughout their care experience.”

excerpt.rendered: Donations from HomeGoods and Homesense shoppers at more than 900 locations nationwide funded cancer research and patient care at Dana-Farber.
