jetpack-related-posts.title: HomeGoods expands support to enhance patient care
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Through HomeGoods’ Find Home Anywhere mission—funded largely by donations from its generous shoppers—HomeGoods and the TJX Foundation have made a three-year commitment to donate at least $3.6 million to Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: HomeGoods Young Adult Lounge is open at Dana-Farber
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The new HomeGoods Young Adult Lounge at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute provides a comfortable, age-appropriate space for adolescent and young adult patients to relax and access resources before and after treatments.

img.alt_text: A group of people participate in a ribbon-cutting ceremony

jetpack-related-posts.title: Creating community for adolescent and young adult patients
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Each day, nearly 50 adolescent and young adult (AYA) patients—those between the ages of 15 and 39—come to Dana-Farber for treatment, but many never connect with one another because they wait for appointments on different floors.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Teen Cancer America Partnership anniversary honored by rock legend Sir Roger Daltrey
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Legendary rock icon Sir Roger Daltrey, lead singer of The Who and co-founder of Teen Cancer America (TCA), visited Dana-Farber Cancer Institute on Aug. 26 to mark the 10th anniversary of Dana-Farber’s partnership with TCA.

img.alt_text: Lindsay Frazier, MD and Sir Roger Daltrey

jetpack-related-posts.title: PopStroke
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: PopStroke completed its second annual October Breast Cancer Awareness Initiative, last year, in partnership with Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund. Throughout October, PopStroke locations nationally ran a number of initiatives to support breast cancer research and patient care at Dana-Farber, raising close to $145,000.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On Sept. 30, Dana-Farber announced the completion of one of the largest-ever fundraising campaigns focused solely on cancer: The Dana-Farber Campaign.

title.rendered: Researchers support research to advance early detection

content.rendered:
Winter 2024
By Nichole Bernier
Photography by Sam Ogden

When Marielle Kaifer lost her mother to lung adenocarcinoma, she wanted a way to honor her mother’s struggle while supporting research to identify early markers of the non-small cell lung cancer so prevalent in her family.

As chemists and researchers themselves, Marielle and her husband, Angel Kaifer, appreciated the importance of seed funding for groundbreaking research. So in 2019, they made a $1 million gift to establish the Barbara Wilson Gomez Endowed Fellowship in Thoracic Oncology at Dana-Farber in the lab of Pasi Jänne, MD, PhD, who was then director of the Lowe Center for Thoracic Oncology and is currently director of the Belfer Center for Applied Cancer Science and of the Chen-Huang Center for EGFR-Mutant Lung Cancers, and the David M. Livingston, MD, Chair at Dana-Farber.

“The quality of communication inspires confidence. You feel involved in what they’re doing, and their progress, and feel your effort is having an effect.”

Marielle Kaifer

Then in 2022 came Angel’s own diagnosis, and with it, their commitment to another cancer in need of better treatment options.

“He had a rarer form of urothelial cancer, in the upper tract of the kidney, and then a very rare pattern of metastasis directly to bone,” said Marielle. “I was struck by how few treatment options were available. And I was very struck by the fact that there seemed to be so many tests coming out for early cancer detection, but not much for urothelial cancer.”

When Angel began treatment at Dana-Farber, he and Marielle were impressed by the work of Joaquim Bellmunt, MD, PhD, director of the Bladder Cancer Center. They recognized another need and opportunity, and launched The Kaifer Family Bladder Cancer Research Fund with a $1.3 million gift to support Bellmunt’s work.

Angel and Marielle’s hope for their funding is that research would enable urothelial cancer patients to be diagnosed sooner than stage II, before there is any substantial metastasis. “They’re looking at detection of cancer through blood analysis, which we think would be a game changer for this type of cancer, because it would facilitate early detection and probably much better outcomes,” said Angel.

“With this funding, my team and I are well-positioned to continue our work in developing a new, non-invasive blood test based on epigenomics, to detect and monitor bladder cancer in patients receiving new treatment options for bladder cancer like immunotherapy and antibody drug conjugates,” said Bellmunt. “I am grateful to Angel and Marielle for their support of this work, which we are hopeful will improve early detection and treatment monitoring.”

In some past donations to medical institutions, Marielle and Angel haven’t always felt well-connected to the projects they were funding. Working with Dana-Farber, they say, has been an entirely different experience because of the open flow of information on achievements made possible by their gifts.

“The quality of communication inspires confidence,” Marielle said. “You feel involved in what they’re doing, and their progress, and feel your effort is having an effect.”

excerpt.rendered: Marielle and Angel Kaifer are supporting Dana-Farber research into a blood test to detect and monitor bladder cancers.

Connolly Small Cell Lung Cancer Research Fund is supporting Jacob Sands, MD, who in collaboration with Matthew Oser, MD, PhD, is exploring new methods to predict…

jetpack-related-posts.title: V is for victory over intractable cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The V Foundation for Cancer Research, founded by legendary basketball coach Jim Valvano, has granted $1.6 million to four Dana-Farber investigators.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Advancing early detection research through the Larry and Susan Marx Fund
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Larry and Susan Marx established the Larry and Susan Marx Fund for Early Detection with a $2.6 million gift, supporting efforts to detect and screen cancers earlier and improve treatment outcomes.

img.alt_text: Susan and Larry Marx in biking gear

jetpack-related-posts.title: Prevention is goal of groundbreaking immunotherapy trial
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: When asked what motivates her to support cancer research, Susan Hertog starts at the beginning, when her best friend was diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer at the age of 49.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Lee and Alexandria Zachos
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Donahues drive research into liquid biopsy for early detection and personalized medicine
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Recently, Digger and Susan made a generous gift of $1 million to the Donahue Family Fund for Prostate Cancer and the Donahue Family Fund for Cancer Interception at Dana-Farber.

title.rendered: First-ever fellowship in metastatic prostate cancer and AI research

content.rendered:
Winter 2024
By Colleen Sullivan
Photography by Michael Blanchard, Sam Ogden

When Tom McDonough was diagnosed with prostate cancer, he and his wife, Olivia, set to work to find the best oncologist in the country to lead his care team. A former health care executive, Tom approached this process the same way he did most things—in a very careful, efficient, and logical manner.

But when the couple met Mary-Ellen Taplin, MD, at Dana-Farber, it came down to a gut feeling.

“I just felt for the first time, ‘this is it, she’s the one,’” said Olivia. “When we walked out of the meeting I said to Tom, ‘She’s gonna be the Tommy Brady of our care team.’ She’s our quarterback.”

Taplin is a world-renowned expert in genitourinary cancer, balancing her time between compassionate patient care and cutting-edge research. Her work has been instrumental in understanding the mechanisms of prostate cancer response and resistance—a crucial component of developing next-generation therapies for this disease.

Inspired by their experiences at Dana-Farber, the McDonoughs wanted to make an impact on prostate cancer research that could change the paradigm of early detection, care management, and treatment for metastatic disease—and they found it in a unique collaboration between Taplin and Eliezer Van Allen, MD, chief of the Division of Population Sciences and the Chandra Nohria Family Chair for AI in Cancer Research at Dana-Farber and an expert in computational biology.

Van Allen’s work focuses on the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to dissect high volumes of complex data directly from cancer patients and uses these insights to address major open questions in the field. He and Taplin are working together to harness the power of AI to accelerate the analysis of prostate cancer’s genomics, disease progression, and treatment resistance, as well as speed the development of novel therapeutic approaches.

Confident that this collaboration would yield results, the McDonoughs made a gift of nearly $1.3 million to establish the McDonough Endowed Fellowship in Metastatic Prostate Cancer Research and Artificial Intelligence—the first-ever fellowship that combines metastatic prostate cancer research with AI research at Dana-Farber.

“Olivia and I are not going to solve the riddle of metastatic prostate cancer, but we can contribute to the solution,” said Tom. “This project may never help me, but down the road there are going to be patients who can benefit. Everything we do in philanthropy is to fund programs that have a tangible impact.”

“Endowed fellowships provide resources that enable Dana-Farber to train the next generation of cancer researchers and clinicians,” said Taplin. “Eli and I are grateful for Tom and Olivia’s support—this fellowship is a unique opportunity and one that we feel will enable further progress in treating this difficult disease.”

excerpt.rendered: Tom and Olivia McDonough’s gift fuels collaboration to harness the power of AI and speed development of novel therapies against prostate cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Grants catalyze new advances in prostate cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Prostate Cancer Foundation has awarded $1.45 million in grants to three Dana-Farber investigators researching more powerful treatments for the disease.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Prostate Cancer Research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Prostate Cancer Research gave nearly $400,000 in support of a Dana-Farber study that aims to improve prostate cancer screening equity. Researchers will analyze the impact of community-targeted interventions to reduce barriers to screening in Black men with prostate cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Prostate Cancer Foundation fuels Dana-Farber innovation with $1M+ in grants
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: PCF recently awarded $1,050,000 to three Dana-Farber Cancer Institute researchers through two Young Investigator Awards and one Challenge Award, each supporting research projects aimed at combating prostate cancer and improving outcomes for patients.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Reaching across the globe to advance prostate cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Through annual gifts and a bequest, Mayer has made a significant gift commitment, establishing The Ross Mayer Endowed Fellowship in Prostate Cancer and the accompanying Mayer Fellow Advancement Fund.

img.alt_text: Three people in a Dana-Farber office

jetpack-related-posts.title: Groundbreaking studies take aim at disparities and advanced disease
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Prostate Cancer Foundation (PCF) has awarded grants totaling more than $2.3 million to Dana-Farber researchers.

jetpack-related-posts.title: National Foundation for Cancer Research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber recently received a $110,000 grant from the National Foundation for Cancer Research to study new, non-invasive approaches to identify specific subtypes of kidney cancer and particular genetic alterations in prostate cancer, with the aim of creating earlier detection and treatment interventions for patients with these diseases.

img.alt_text: National Foundation for Cancer Research logo

title.rendered: AACR targets breast and uterine cancers

content.rendered:
Winter 2024
By Kathy Clute
Photography by Sam Ogden

Breast and uterine cancers are the focus of more than $1 million in grants to four Dana-Farber investigators recently awarded by the American Association for Cancer Research (AACR) and its partners.

Nolan Priedigkeit, MD, PhD, and Capucine Héraud, PhD, received grants to support their research into breast cancer. Sarah Johnstone, MD, PhD, and Joyce Liu, MD, MPH, director of clinical research in the Division of Gynecology, received awards for their investigations of uterine cancer.

“We are honored to support the innovative research at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, which represents AACR’s commitment to advancing the fight against breast and uterine cancers,” said Yixian (John) Zhang, PhD, vice president of research and grants administration at the AACR. “By funding these promising studies, we aim to foster the development of targeted, effective treatments that can significantly improve patient outcomes.”

Priedigkeit is testing a new technology to target metastatic breast cancer cells by focusing on nucleic acids like RNA instead of proteins, an approach that could lead to more effective and less toxic treatments. He will test an RNA sensor that can detect fusion RNAs, activate a molecular switch, and trigger a toxin within cancer cells while leaving normal cells unharmed. His grant—a Young Investigator Award for Translational Cancer Research—is from the AACR and Conquer Cancer®, the ASCO Foundation.

Héraud received an AACR-Lobular Breast Cancer Alliance Invasive Lobular Carcinoma Research Fellowship for her work to better understand the effectiveness of hormone treatments for that subtype of breast cancer. She will study breast cancer tissue samples from early stage invasive lobular carcinomas and invasive ductal carcinomas to identify the differences between them, testing how they respond to tamoxifen and another hormone therapy, letrozole.

“By funding these promising studies, we aim to foster the development of targeted, effective treatments that can significantly improve patient outcomes.”

YixiaN Zhang, PhD, American Association for Cancer Research

Uterine cancer is one of the few cancers where both incidence and mortality are rising. Liu is investigating whether a combination therapy that inhibits two key proteins, WEE1 and ATR, could have synergistic effects that would improve outcomes for patients diagnosed with these cancers. Liu received a Victoria’s Secret Global Fund for Women’s Cancers Rising Innovator Research Grant, in partnership with Pelotonia and AACR.

Johnstone, who received a Victoria’s Secret Global Fund for Women’s Cancers Career Development Award, in partnership with Pelotonia and AACR, is targeting difficult gynecologic cancers by studying the 3D organization of the genome to determine how certain proteins are disrupted and how they contribute to cancer development.

title.rendered: Falmouth Road Race: Pacing the way forward against cancer

content.rendered:
Winter 2024
By Nichole Bernier
Photography by Steve McLaughlin

The scenic ASICS Falmouth Road Race, winding seven miles along the Cape Cod coast, is one of the most esteemed running events of the summer, with bib numbers highly sought after by global elite racers and local joggers alike. Now in its 52nd year, the race is also a powerful fundraising vehicle for runners making strides toward defying cancer.

On August 18, 352 athletes represented Dana-Farber on the Falmouth route, raising nearly $1 million and adding to the historic achievements of The Dana-Farber Campaign.

One of these runners, Amber Miller, understands cancer from both sides of the infusion chair. As a teen, she was treated in Dana-Farber’s Jimmy Fund Clinic and underwent a bone marrow transplant during her sophomore year of college. Now a nurse practitioner in the Jimmy Fund Clinic, she takes care of children and young adults.

“My own cancer experience and the incredible care I received at Dana-Farber inspired me to help other patients on their cancer journeys,” she said. However, she didn’t expect it to inspire her for another round, this time for breast cancer, shortly after running her first Falmouth Road Race in 2022.

“I underwent chemotherapy, two surgeries, and 30 days of radiation. As a young wife and mom, I was terrified,” she said. “But just like my first experience all those years ago, my care team had a plan for me and provided wisdom and support.” Amber was grateful to be joined by her husband, CJ, for this year’s race.

Dana Finn ran her first Falmouth Road Race this year in honor of her mother, who had a rare form of bile duct cancer 10 years ago. She was inspired to join the effort by her 16-year-old son Nate, who took up running at age 12 during the COVID-19 pandemic. As of 2024, he has completed four Falmouth Road Races for Dana-Farber.

“I wanted to give back to the institution that gave my mother the best treatment available and treated her with dignity and the utmost compassion,” Dana said. “Spending time with my son working towards a mutual goal is incredibly rewarding.”

Nate was thrilled to have his mom join him this time around. “I’m excited to run and fundraise with my mom in my grandmother’s honor and to support other Dana-Farber patients.”

Dana-Farber and the Jimmy Fund is the official Legacy Partner of Falmouth’s charity program, Numbers for Nonprofits, which has helped raise more than $71 million for charities since 2000, including more than $11 million for Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber team defies cancer in ASICS Falmouth Road Race
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On Aug. 21, more than 330 members of Dana-Farber’s team ran seven miles along the scenic Cape Cod coastline for the 50th running of the ASICS Falmouth Road Race.

img.alt_text: Falmouth Road Race Team Power runners

jetpack-related-posts.title: A record-breaking year for Dana-Farber’s ASICS Falmouth Road Race team
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: This year, on August 17, runners from Dana-Farber’s 2025 Falmouth Road Race team raised a record-breaking $1,105,554.90, the highest fundraising total in the team’s 23-year history, which exceeds $12.5 million to date for innovative research and compassionate patient care.

img.alt_text: Falmouth Road Race team in Dana-Farber gear

jetpack-related-posts.title: Falmouth Road Race team surpasses $10 million milestone
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On August 20, more than 325 participants laced up on behalf of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute to compete in the ASICS Falmouth Road Race.

img.alt_text: A Falmouth Road Race runner poses for a photo

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Jimmy Fund celebrates 75 years
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On May 22, 1948, Einar Gustafson, a young boy being treated for lymphoma by Dr. Sidney Farber and dubbed “Jimmy” to protect his privacy, shared his story from his hospital bed.

img.alt_text: The original Jimmy in a hospital bed with an old TV

jetpack-related-posts.title: Runners across the country race for Dana-Farber and the Jimmy Fund
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The 2022 Run Any Race season roster consisted of 71 runners, running various races across the globe in support of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund.

img.alt_text: Andrew Kaczysnki of Team Beans on the course

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber’s Boston half team sets new record
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Sunday, November 9, marked the Boston Athletic Association’s (B.A.A.’s) annual Boston Half, a scenic 13.1-mile race through Franklin Park and the Emerald Necklace Park System.

title.rendered: Meet the new Co-Chairs of the Jimmy Fund: Brock Holt and Tom Caron

content.rendered:
Winter 2024
By Nathalie Sczublewski
Photography by John Deputy

In August, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute named former Boston Red Sox player Brock Holt and NESN anchor Tom Caron to serve as Co-Chairs of the Jimmy Fund.

In this role, Holt and Caron will be the lead ambassadors and public spokespeople on behalf of the Jimmy Fund. They will strengthen relationships with professional sports teams, strategize on fundraising initiatives, celebrate the tremendous community of passionate Jimmy Fund supporters, emphasize the importance of philanthropic support for Dana-Farber, and highlight the achievements of Dana-Farber doctors and researchers as they strive to find cures and treatments for cancer.

Holt, nicknamed “The Brock Star,” was a utility player for the Red Sox from 2013 to 2019. He served as the Jimmy Fund Captain from 2015 to 2019 and is a long-time supporter of Dana-Farber’s fundraising efforts. Caron has been a member of NESN’s Red Sox broadcast team and host of pre- and post-game shows for more than two decades. He has been involved in Jimmy Fund events including the WEEI/NESN Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon for more than 20 years.

Since 1948, a handful of passionate and dedicated individuals held this leadership role, including Bill Koster (1948-1977), one of the founders of the Jimmy Fund who was known as “Mr. Jimmy Fund”; legendary broadcaster Ken Coleman (1978-1984); Red Sox infielder Mike Andrews (1984-2009); and former Red Sox president and CEO and Worcester Red Sox chairman, the late Larry Lucchino, who served as Chairman of the Jimmy Fund from 2016 until his passing in April 2024.

“It is an honor to follow in Larry’s footsteps to help grow the storied partnership between the Boston Red Sox and Dana-Farber’s Jimmy Fund,” said Holt. “I want to continue to help raise awareness and funds for cancer research and care in any way I can. Some of my earliest memories are coming to Red Sox games as a kid and dropping change in the Jimmy Fund can.”

“To be Co- Chair of this incredible philanthropic organization is truly humbling,” said Caron. “I’ve witnessed the lifesaving work done at Dana-Farber over the years and have seen the direct impact of fundraising efforts like the Radio-Telethon. I’m also a former patient, after a lymphoma diagnosis in 2015. I can’t wait to work alongside Brock, a tireless advocate of the Jimmy Fund, and help lead the charge to strike out cancer.”

excerpt.rendered: Holt and Caron will be the lead ambassadors and public spokespeople on behalf of the Jimmy Fund, helping to raise funds and awareness.

jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On Oct. 6, 2025, Jimmy Fund Co-Chairs Tom Caron and Brock Holt hosted the inaugural Jimmy Fund Pro-Am Golf Tournament at the Tournament Players Club (TPC) Boston.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon breaks records with $5.7 million raised for Dana-Farber
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The WEEI/NESN Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon presented by Arbella Insurance continued to be a beacon of support for Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund in August with a record-breaking fundraising year.

img.alt_text: Ali Kelleher cheering at Fenway Park

jetpack-related-posts.title: Expect Miracles Foundation honored with the Boston Red Sox Jimmy Fund Award
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Expect Miracles Foundation (EMF) received the 2025 Boston Red Sox Jimmy Fund Award—the Jimmy Fund’s highest honor—during a special on-field ceremony at Fenway Park.

img.alt_text: Group photo of Jimmy Fund Award winners and Dana-Farber staff at Fenway Park

jetpack-related-posts.title: Another home run year for the Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The WEEI/NESN Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon presented by Arbella Insurance helped strike out cancer for the 22nd year at Fenway Park in August, raising nearly $4 million for adult and pediatric cancer care and research at Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Red Sox name 2023 Jimmy Fund Captain

jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Boston Red Sox pitcher, Garrett Whitlock, has been named Jimmy Fund Captain for the 2023 baseball season.

title.rendered: V Foundation boosts pediatric AML research

content.rendered:
Winter 2024
By Kathy Clute
Photography by Sam Ogden

The V Foundation for Cancer Research is taking aim at acute myeloid leukemia (AML) in children with an $800,000 grant that will enhance the search for more effective and durable treatments for the disease.

Scott Armstrong, MD, PhD, chair of the Department of Pediatric Oncology at Dana-Farber and the David G. Nathan, MD, Professor of Pediatrics, is the recipient of a four-year Pediatric Translational Research Grant from the foundation. Armstrong, who also serves as the Institute’s senior vice president for drug discovery and chief research strategy officer, directs a 20-person lab that is focused on developing new therapies for childhood cancers.

AML is a particularly challenging type of leukemia to treat, especially in children, who have had to rely on toxic chemotherapy and bone marrow transplants for decades. A new class of drugs called menin inhibitors, which can be taken orally, has shown real promise for treating difficult subtypes of AML. However, disease resistance develops in some patients when the menin gene mutates during treatment.

“We’ve documented the mutations and are now trying to find ways to overcome and possibly prevent the disease from becoming drug resistant,” said Armstrong, who is researching next-generation menin inhibitors and treatments. “We hope that our work will eventually make chemotherapy unnecessary by bringing menin inhibitors and other targeted therapies into the standard of care for children with newly diagnosed or refractory AML.”

The V Foundation was founded in 1993 by ESPN and famed basketball coach Jim Valvano with the mission of achieving victory over cancer. It has supported pioneering cancer research at Dana-Farber for nearly 30 years. 

“It is exciting to contemplate the transformation in pediatric AML treatment that could come out of Dr. Armstrong’s lab.”

Kara Coleman, PhD, V Foundation for Cancer Research

“We fund the best ideas from the best cancer researchers in the country so that they can make discoveries that benefit cancer patients everywhere,” said Kara Coleman, PhD, vice president of grants and research at the V Foundation. “It is exciting to contemplate the transformation in pediatric AML treatment that could come out of Dr. Armstrong’s lab.”

jetpack-related-posts.title: Children’s Cancer Research Fund
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Children’s Cancer Research Fund awarded their Emerging Scientist Award to Dana-Farber pediatric oncologist Emily Heikamp, MD, PhD, MSc. The grant of $100,000 will support Heikamp’s work in uncovering therapeutic vulnerabilities in the NU98-r gene, which could lead to safer and more effective treatments for children with relapsed acute myeloid leukemia.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Gabrielle’s Angel Foundation for Cancer Research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Gabrielle’s Angel Foundation for Cancer Research awarded $250,000 to Dana-Farber’s Zuzana Tothova, MD, PhD, who is exploring the biology of cohesin mutations, frequent and recurrent drivers of myelodysplastic syndromes and acute myeloid leukemia. With this funding, Tothova aims to develop targeted treatments for these cancers.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Alex’s Lemonade Stand Foundation targets childhood cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In 2000, a 4-year-old girl named Alexandra “Alex” Scott set up a lemonade stand to raise money for research into childhood cancers like hers.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Rally Foundation supports bold pediatric cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Rally Foundation for Childhood Cancer Research recently awarded $450,000 in grants to four Dana-Farber researchers developing innovative treatments for pediatric cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Leukemia & Lymphoma Society attacks rare and resistant blood cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Leukemia & Lymphoma Society (LLS) has awarded six grants totaling $5.8 million to Dana-Farber investigators.

This generous grant supports her research focused on determining whether targeting two proteins can effectively treat a specific type of acute myeloid leukemia. title.rendered: Cancer biologist Edward Chouchani receives Emerging Leader grant

content.rendered:
Winter 2024
By Kathy Clute
Photography by Sam Ogden

The Mark Foundation for Cancer Research has awarded a $750,000 Emerging Leader Award to Edward Chouchani, PhD, to build on his groundbreaking discovery that a substance long thought to be an inert byproduct of cell growth and division actually plays a key role in controlling cell proliferation.

For almost a century, scientists believed that lactate—prevalent in rapidly growing and metastatic cancers—was merely a byproduct of glycolysis, one of the ways cells produce energy as they grow and divide. But Chouchani’s lab has established that the molecule is a critical metabolic signal in cancer cells.

Chouchani and his team in the Department of Cancer Biology use mass spectrometry and biochemical approaches to understand how metabolites regulate cellular function in pre-clinical models of health and disease. They have spent years developing new techniques to learn which proteins respond directly to sharp rises in lactate and studying the basic biochemical mechanisms involved.

“We now know that lactate plays an active part in helping cancer cells grow by binding directly to a core regulator of cell cycle,” said Chouchani. “With this funding from The Mark Foundation, we will systematically characterize the mechanisms and targets through which lactate can regulate tumor growth and metastasis. We hope this will open up new possibilities for cancer treatment.”

Mark Foundation CEO Ryan Schoenfeld, PhD, noted that the organization’s Emerging Leader Award “enables the next generation of oncology superstars to take more risks at an earlier stage of their career by pursuing innovative projects that might never launch without our support.”

Founded in 2017, The Mark Foundation partners with scientists worldwide to accelerate research that will transform cancer prevention, diagnosis, and treatment. It has awarded more than $220 million in grants to investigators at more than 100 academic institutions in 16 countries.

excerpt.rendered: The Mark Foundation grant advances groundbreaking research which revealed a substance long thought to be inert actually plays a key role in cell proliferation.

jetpack-related-posts.title: American Federation for Aging Research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Glenn Foundation for Medical Research and the American Federation for Aging Research awarded a $300,000 grant to support basic science research by Dana-Farber’s Edward Chouchani, PhD, as he seeks to systematically define the functional targets of reactive oxygen species that contribute to longevity and age.

img.alt_text: Glenn Foundation and American Federation for Aging Research

jetpack-related-posts.title: Grant fuels research into the new field of immunometabolism
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With funding from the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative, Dana-Farber seeks to better understand and manipulate immunometabolism, which is emerging as an important frontier with potential to advance treatments for metabolic and inflammatory diseases including cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: V Foundation grants power colorectal cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The V Foundation for Cancer Research once again demonstrated its remarkable generosity and commitment to advancing cancer research at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute by awarding $1.4 million in grants to two exceptional investigators.

jetpack-related-posts.title: High-risk, high-reward research is The Mathers Foundation’s priority
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Transformative basic research is the focus of The G. Harold and Leila Y. Mathers Charitable Foundation, which recently awarded $1.5 million to fund Dana-Farber research on unraveling the inner workings of human cells.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Trustee Science Committee fosters the next generation of researchers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Shelby Roseman, PhD, and Amanda Smythers, PhD, were recently named the latest group of Trustee Science Committee Postdoctoral Fellows at Dana-Farber.

img.alt_text: Liquid pouring from a beaker into a petri dish

jetpack-related-posts.title: V Foundation boosts pediatric AML research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The V Foundation is taking aim at acute myeloid leukemia in children with a grant that will enhance Dana-Farber's search for more effective and durable treatments.

title.rendered: Jimmy Fund Scooper Bowl® presented by Herb Chambers

content.rendered:
Winter 2024
By Sofi Elbadawi
Photography by Sasha Pedro

Stack those cups! Enthusiasts of Jimmy Fund Scooper Bowl® presented by Herb Chambers raised over $410,000 to benefit Dana-Farber patients and families. Over three sunny days in June, more than 10,000 attendees gathered to enjoy unlimited ice cream, with proceeds supporting The Dana-Farber Campaign’s mission to defy cancer. This year marked the return of Jimmy Fund Scooper Bowl to Boston’s City Hall Plaza for the first time since 2019. The beautifully re-designed plaza was the perfect backdrop for New England’s sweetest kickoff to summer.

Jimmy Fund Scooper Bowl is the nation’s largest all-you-can-eat ice cream festival, and this year’s event featured more than 14 unique ice cream partners. With the help of national staples like Ben & Jerry’s® and Tillamook® and local favorites like Holy Cow Ice Cream Café and Bliss Premium Ice Cream, over 900 gallons of ice cream were brought in.

To close out the three-day long festivities, ice cream lovers 21 years and up were able to enjoy more top creameries, along with two drink tickets, inside the Scoop at Night tent. Thanks to the support of ticketholders, sponsors, and volunteers, this year’s Jimmy Fund Scooper Bowl and Scoop at Night were a sweet success, with critical funds raised to help conquer cancer once and for all.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Scooper Bowl® celebrates 40 years of support for Dana-Farber
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Ice cream lovers of all ages were invited to Patriot Place in Foxborough, Mass., to celebrate the 40th annual Jimmy Fund Scooper Bowl® presented by Valvoline Instant Oil ChangeSM.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Two longstanding supporters receive the Jimmy Fund’s highest honor
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The 2024 Boston Red Sox Jimmy Fund Award was presented to The Herb Chambers Companies and Team Beans at a special Fenway Park ceremony.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Scooper Bowl®
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: More than 15,000 ice cream lovers flocked to Boston’s City Hall Plaza in June for the nation’s largest all-you-can-eat ice cream festival, Jimmy Fund Scooper Bowl®, and its 21+ happy hour, Scoop at Night. Thanks to devoted partners Ben & Jerry’s, Brigham’s, Edy’s, Friendly’s, Häagen-Dazs, Holy Cow, Hood, JonnyPops, Lactaid,…

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Herb Chambers Companies surpasses $1 million in gifts
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Herb Chambers Companies, one of New England’s largest auto dealers, has been a powerful ally and supporter of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund since 2015.

img.alt_text: Herb Chambers and his partner, Melissa Lees, with the cow she created, Chin Up, during the CowParade New England Preview Party.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Arbella plays an MVP role in the Jimmy Fund’s mission to strike out cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A longtime partner of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund, Arbella Insurance Group continued its steadfast support of Dana-Farber’s mission throughout 2023, living out the company’s motto of: “Here. For Good.”

img.alt_text: A group of people holding an over-sized check at Fenway Park

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Herb Chambers Companies
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Herb Chambers Companies continued their support of Dana-Farber as Premier Sponsor of the Jimmy Fund in 2024. Their continued partnership has been felt across marquee Jimmy Fund events since 2015, resulting in over $1 million of cumulative support for Dana-Farber.

title.rendered: Alka Ohri Foundation enhances holistic breast cancer care

content.rendered:
Winter 2024
By Cyrena Musset
Photography by Nipun Sarin

The Alka Ohri Foundation is committed to enhancing the lives of patients with breast cancer by supporting programs that focus on holistic wellbeing throughout all levels of treatment. To this end, the foundation recently pledged $100,000 to aid Dana-Farber’s Leonard P. Zakim Center for Integrative Therapies and Healthy Living in launching a Personalized Healthy Living Program for breast cancer patients. The program is designed to preserve participants’ strength, endurance, and mobility throughout the breast cancer continuum.

The foundation’s funding will allow Jennifer Ligibel, MD, director of the Zakim Center, to leverage ongoing research and clinical care and rapidly generate data on the role of diet, exercise, and additional holistic programs in this patient population. She ultimately seeks to develop an evidence-informed, aggregated model that draws from the most effective elements of the program and builds a blueprint for the incorporation of healthy living programs into oncology clinics across the globe.

“I extend my heartfelt gratitude to the Alka Ohri Foundation for their generous, forward-thinking gift,” said Ligibel.

excerpt.rendered: A recent grant will help launch a personalized program designed to preserve patients’ strength, endurance, and mobility throughout the breast cancer continuum.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Terri Brodeur Breast Cancer Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Terri Brodeur Breast Cancer Foundation gave $125,000 in support of research led by Paolo Tarantino, MD, which seeks to improve the precision of antibody-drug conjugates. This funding will aid Tarantino in unlocking new insights into metastatic breast cancer, with the intention of identifying additional treatments for patients.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Expanding equitable access to critical care
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Last year, the National Breast Cancer Foundation (NBCF) generously provided $155,000 to support Dana-Farber’s inclusion, diversity, and equity work to ensure equitable health outcomes for all.

img.alt_text: National Breast Cancer Foundation, Inc. Logo

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Terri Brodeur Breast Cancer Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Terri Brodeur Breast Cancer Foundation awarded $125,000 to Genevra Kuziel, PhD, supporting her research on estrogen receptor-positive (ER+) breast cancer, the most common breast cancer subtype with a high recurrence rate. Kuziel’s work aims to develop innovative combination therapies, with the goal of transforming treatment options and improving outcomes…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Breast Cancer Research Foundation continues support with nearly $4 million in grants
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Since its founding by the late Evelyn Lauder alongside her dear friend Larry Norton, MD, in 1993, the Breast Cancer Research Foundation (BCRF) has championed research as the key to one day curing breast cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Legacy of Leadership and Hope: The Elaine and Eduardo Saverin Foundation’s generational commitment to patients with metastatic breast cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Elaine and Eduardo Saverin Foundation has made an extraordinary $20 million grant to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute to accelerate research and care for people living with stage IV breast cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Cancer Couch Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Cancer Couch Foundation has granted $225,000 to support the work of Daniel Abravanel, MD, PhD. The funds will drive Abravanel’s research on how drug resistance arises in metastatic breast cancer and foster the development of innovative strategies for improving treatments for patients with this challenging form of the disease.

content.rendered:
Winter 2024
By Lori Dougherty

Bradley McGregor, MD, was recognized as the inaugural incumbent of the Marra Lochiatto Investigatorship in Kidney Cancer Research at Dana-Farber during an event in May. McGregor is the director of clinical research in the Lank Center for Genitourinary Oncology at Dana-Farber, specializing in kidney cancer and other genitourinary malignancies. Endowed by Ken Lochiatto and his family in loving memory of his wife, Marra, this prestigious investigatorship is a powerful investment in The Dana-Farber Campaign and enables McGregor to pursue high-risk, high-reward kidney cancer research that has the potential to change the paradigm of this disease for patients around the world.

excerpt.rendered: This prestigious investigatorship enables McGregor to pursue high-risk, high-reward kidney cancer research with potential to change the paradigm of this disease.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Bekensteins endow investigatorship in honor of Meredith and Billy Starr
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Bekensteins recently made a generous gift to the Institute to establish the Meredith and Billy Starr Investigatorship.

img.alt_text: Billy Starr and Meredith Beaton Starr

jetpack-related-posts.title: Tim and Ginny Bliss endow investigatorship with $2.2 million gift
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber's Bing Center for Waldenström’s Macroglobulinemia is the world’s largest referral center for a rare blood cancer that occurs in only about 1,500 patients each year. Tim Bliss, of Santa Barbara, California, is one of them.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Lindsley named Edward P. Evans Investigator
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Coleman Lindsley, MD, PhD, was recognized as the Edward P. Evans Investigator in MDS research at Dana-Farber at an event in 2023.

img.alt_text: Coleman Lindsley and Michael D. Lewis pose for a photo with a framed lab coat at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute

jetpack-related-posts.title: Freedman named to David Goldstein Chair
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Matthew Freedman, MD, was named the inaugural incumbent of the David Goldstein Chair at Dana-Farber, endowed by the late Jonathan Goldstein to support kidney cancer research in memory of his father, David Goldstein.

img.alt_text: Matthew Freedman and his family at an event

jetpack-related-posts.title: Devoted sister endows research fellowship for kidney cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Maura Shaughnessy has been a steadfast Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC) rider for nearly 31 years, raising more than $2.8 million, but one thing she loves even more than cycling is her brother Frank.

img.alt_text: Frank and Maura Shaughnessy on a bike ride

jetpack-related-posts.title: National Foundation for Cancer Research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber recently received a $110,000 grant from the National Foundation for Cancer Research to study new, non-invasive approaches to identify specific subtypes of kidney cancer and particular genetic alterations in prostate cancer, with the aim of creating earlier detection and treatment interventions for patients with these diseases.

img.alt_text: National Foundation for Cancer Research logo

content.rendered:
Winter 2024
By Kayla McMahon

In 2009, Laura Smith launched a fundraiser with her friend Jill, who had recently been diagnosed with ovarian cancer. Together, they selected the name girlygirl P.A.R.T.S. 5K/Walk for Ovarian Cancer, with the acronym representing their fundraising mission—Prescreening Awareness Required To Silence ovarian cancer.

Laura and many other dedicated committee members including Trish Cundiff and Erica Kuenzel have kept Jill’s legacy alive by continuing to host this fundraiser annually since she passed away in 2015. They recently celebrated a new milestone—raising over $1 million in support of ovarian cancer research at Dana-Farber under the direction of Ursula Matulonis, MD—and are committed to continuing this effort until outcomes are improved for all ovarian cancer patients.

excerpt.rendered: The girlygirl P.A.R.T.S. 5K/Walk for Ovarian Cancer has surpassed $1 million in total funds raised since 2009, supporting research at Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Johnston gift paves the way for a novel ovarian cancer clinical trial
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Debbie Johnston is dedicated to supporting causes that are close to her heart, and Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s ovarian cancer research is one such cause.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Minnesota Ovarian Cancer Alliance
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Ovarian cancer is often difficult to treat at later stages and difficult to detect at earlier stages. With a $100,000 grant, the Minnesota Ovarian Cancer Alliance is supporting research at Dana-Farber into the development of an ultrasensitive blood test to detect ovarian cancer at its earliest, and most treatable, stages.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Kicks for Cancer harnesses power of community to drive cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Nearly 20 years ago, Concord-Carlisle High School hosted its first Kicks for Cancer soccer match to honor the memory of Lois Wells, the mother of assistant men’s soccer coach Steve Wells, who passed away from ovarian cancer. Today, Kicks for Cancer has grown into a vibrant week-long celebration that unites…

img.alt_text: Soccer players mid-game on the field

jetpack-related-posts.title: Campbells advance research into rare ovarian cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Emily Campbell was just 32 when she began seeing doctors in her hometown of Miami for vague symptoms—abdominal discomfort and bloating, low appetite, fatigue—that were dismissed by her local medical team until she insisted on an ultrasound scan.

jetpack-related-posts.title: DeFeo gift aims to push ovarian cancer treatment to next level
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The late Dara Frigoletto DeFeo was a giver, her husband, Peter DeFeo, recalls fondly. Whether it was reading to small children in Dana-Farber’s Jimmy Fund Clinic or helping a senior citizen pluck an item off a high shelf at the grocery store, Dara “had a unique way to communicate that…

img.alt_text: A close-up photo of Dara Frigoletto DeFeo

jetpack-related-posts.title: Gift to ovarian cancer inspired by story of research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In early 2022, Dr. Jean Kasmer read a story in Impact about an ovarian cancer survivor who gave to support the research of Ursula Matulonis, MD, chief of the division of Gynecologic Oncology and the Brock-Wilson Family Chair at Dana-Farber.

title.rendered: Two longstanding supporters receive the Jimmy Fund’s highest honor

content.rendered:
Winter 2024
By Kayla McMahon
Photography by Grace Beal/Boston Red Sox

The 2024 Boston Red Sox Jimmy Fund Award—the Jimmy Fund’s highest honor—was presented to The Herb Chambers Companies and Team Beans in August.

Herb Chambers has been a partner of the Jimmy Fund since 2015. They have supported numerous events and programs over the years, including the 2024 Jimmy Fund Scooper Bowl®, and officially surpassed $1 million in cumulative giving in 2023.

Andrew Kaczynski and Rachel Ensign formed Team Beans in memory of their daughter, Francesca, who was affectionately known as “Beans.” Francesca passed away from a rare brain tumor at 9 months old in 2020. Team Beans has raised over $3.5 million to support infant brain cancer research at Dana-Farber through the Pan-Mass Challenge, along with the Boston Marathon® and New York City Marathon.

excerpt.rendered: The 2024 Boston Red Sox Jimmy Fund Award was presented to The Herb Chambers Companies and Team Beans at a special Fenway Park ceremony.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Larry Lucchino receives Jimmy Fund’s highest honor
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The 2023 Boston Red Sox Jimmy Fund Award was presented to Chairman of the Jimmy Fund Larry Lucchino at a special Fenway Park ceremony in August.

img.alt_text: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute trustee Larry Lucchino with Dana-Farber CEO Dr. Laurie Glimcher

jetpack-related-posts.title: Boston Red Sox Jimmy Fund Award
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The 2022 Boston Red Sox Jimmy Fund Award—the Jimmy Fund’s highest honor—was presented to John Berardi (second from right), program director of Jimmy Fund Little League presented by Franklin Sports, which rallies thousands of youth baseball and softball players each summer to fundraise for the Jimmy Fund in their communities…

img.alt_text: People on the field at Fenway Park

jetpack-related-posts.title: Expect Miracles Foundation honored with the Boston Red Sox Jimmy Fund Award
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Expect Miracles Foundation (EMF) received the 2025 Boston Red Sox Jimmy Fund Award—the Jimmy Fund’s highest honor—during a special on-field ceremony at Fenway Park.

img.alt_text: Group photo of Jimmy Fund Award winners and Dana-Farber staff at Fenway Park

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Herb Chambers Companies surpasses $1 million in gifts
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Herb Chambers Companies, one of New England’s largest auto dealers, has been a powerful ally and supporter of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund since 2015.

img.alt_text: Herb Chambers and his partner, Melissa Lees, with the cow she created, Chin Up, during the CowParade New England Preview Party.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Arbella plays an MVP role in the Jimmy Fund’s mission to strike out cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A longtime partner of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund, Arbella Insurance Group continued its steadfast support of Dana-Farber’s mission throughout 2023, living out the company’s motto of: “Here. For Good.”

img.alt_text: A group of people holding an over-sized check at Fenway Park

jetpack-related-posts.title: CowParade New England MOOves the needle
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The cows of CowParade New England presented by Herb Chambers are MOOving to new pastures after a successful, summer-long event celebrating the Jimmy Fund’s 75th anniversary with the Greater Boston community.

img.alt_text: People pose with colorful umbrellas and a dog in front of a painted cow sculpture

content.rendered:
Winter 2024
By Stephanie Lowitt
Photography by Steve Gilbert

The Dana-Farber community is celebrating a momentous achievement that speaks volumes about the strength and dedication of our supporters: together, we have reached our ambitious Campaign goal of 2,000 Dana-Farber Society members. The Dana-Farber Society honors those who have made a legacy gift to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, the Jimmy Fund, the Friends of Dana-Farber, or the Pan-Mass Challenge through a gift in their will, a beneficiary designation, a life income gift, or other planned gift. The generosity and foresight of these donors will help Dana-Farber save the lives of cancer patients far into the future.

excerpt.rendered: The Dana-Farber Society honor those who have made a legacy gift, helping to secure future progress for Dana-Farber research and care.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Society
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Dana-Farber Society (DFS) is a group of visionary donors who are changing lives and creating a legacy through a planned gift such as a bequest, life income gift, or beneficiary designation to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, the Jimmy Fund, the Friends of Dana-Farber, or the Pan-Mass Challenge.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber Society Dinner
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On May 24, more than 200 guests gathered at the Four Seasons Hotel Boston for the annual Dana-Farber Society Dinner.

img.alt_text: Attendees of the Dana-Farber Society Dinner pose for a photo

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Dana-Farber Campaign has inspired pivotal planned gifts that will make a true difference for children and adults with cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Deserving Salute
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: After more than a decade at the helm of Philanthropy Communications at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, Assistant Vice President, Joyce Gallagher is embarking on her retirement journey.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber Presidential Symposium
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: “Sparking Discoveries Through the Power of Community” was the theme for the annual Dana-Farber Cancer Institute Presidential Symposium in October 2023

content.rendered:
Winter 2024
By Kathy Clute
Photography by Josh Campbell

Dana-Farber has a unique tool to foster innovation—the Faculty Research Fund (FRF). When a donor makes a gift for a designated research program or project, 10% of that gift is allotted to the FRF to fuel discoveries across the Institute.

This pool of funds ensures that promising early stage inquiries receive valuable start-up resources, that investigators can push the boundaries of current knowledge, and that Dana-Farber can continue recruiting and retaining the world’s best cancer physicians and scientists.

In Fiscal Year 2024, Dana-Farber allocated just over $9 million to the FRF for institutional priorities that transcend individual disciplines and facilitate breakthroughs across all cancer types. The FRF has deployed more than $75 million to advance our research mission since it was established in 2013.

Projects funded this year include Profile, a large-scale initiative that has assembled one of the world’s most comprehensive databases of the genetic abnormalities that cause tumors to develop and grow. Profile facilitates “precision medicine” (or personalized medicine) by helping physicians match targeted therapies to individual patients based on their cancer’s genomic profile. These therapies are engineered to attack tumor cells with specific abnormalities, while leaving normal cells largely unharmed.

The FRF also supported research devoted to inherited (germline) mutations that may indicate whether an individual and close relatives are at increased risk for certain cancers, and the Center for Precision Immuno-Oncology (CPIO). The CPIO enables translational, multi-department research among Dana-Farber’s laboratory and clinical investigators as well as with external academic and industry partners. Above all, the FRF ensures we are prioritizing the needs of our faculty—the brilliant minds behind every scientific breakthrough that brings us closer to a world without cancer.

excerpt.rendered: The Faculty Research Fund supports Dana-Farber priorities that transcend individual disciplines and facilitate breakthroughs across all cancer types.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Faculty Research Fund fuels discovery
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Ten years ago, Dana-Farber leaders created the Faculty Research Fund (FRF), a unique financing mechanism that pools philanthropic resources to accelerate bold scientific discovery.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dale Fishman
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dale Fishman gave $243,000 to fuel pioneering research led by Andrew Aguirre, MD, PhD; Catherine Wu, MD; and physician-scientists across Dana-Farber. Fishman’s multifaceted philanthropy is empowering these investigators to advance novel cellular therapies for pancreatic cancer and personalized cancer vaccines, while bolstering the Faculty Research Fund, which together pave the…

img.alt_text: Liquid pouring from a beaker into a petri dish

jetpack-related-posts.title: Eisenson encourages CGAs as a simple and lasting legacy
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Supporting cancer research and care at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute can take many forms that benefit both the Institute and the donor. Michael Eisenson (pictured), Institute Trustee and chair of The Dana-Farber Campaign, recently established a charitable gift annuity (CGA) with a generous gift of $250,000.

img.alt_text: Michael Eisenson at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute's healing garden

jetpack-related-posts.title: Mindy Green
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With a $100,000 gift, Mindy Green established the Li Li Family EGFR Lung Cancer Research Fund in memory of her mother, Li Li. The fund realizes Li Li’s intention to make a gift to Dana-Farber and will support the cutting-edge research of her thoracic oncologist, Michael Rabin, MD.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Georgette and John Heerwagen
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Georgette and John Heerwagen recently renewed their support for lung cancer research at Dana-Farber with a generous gift of $125,000. Under the direction of David Jackman, MD, in collaboration with David Barbie, MD, both faculty in the Lowe Center for Thoracic Oncology at Dana-Farber, this funding will enable researchers to…

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Ambrose Monell Foundation fuels critical immunotherapy priorities
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: By encouraging strategic risk-taking and rewarding experimentation and new ideas, the Ambrose Monell Foundation is empowering Dana-Farber to capitalize on its collective expertise to develop a new generation of innovative cancer-fighting immunotherapies tailored to the specific needs of patients.

content.rendered:
Winter 2024
By Stephanie Lowitt
Photography by John Deputy

Five things to consider before December 31!

Make a gift that’s matched

Take advantage of our year-end matching challenge to support cancer patients. When you donate to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund today, your gift doubles, thanks to a matching challenge from Arbella Insurance Group. And if your new year’s resolution is to start a monthly gift, all your 2025 payments will be matched, up to $10,000!

Stock and Securities

If you give a gift of appreciated securities before the end of the calendar year, you may be entitled to a federal income tax charitable deduction on this year’s taxes and may also avoid capital gains tax on the appreciation of the asset. And a gift of stock could increase the value of your gift to Dana-Farber and the Jimmy Fund at a decreased cost to you. Through a partnership with The Boston Foundation, you can also donate privately held C-Corp stock for the benefit of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute.

Individual Retirement Account (IRA)

If you are 70½ or older, you can give up to $105,000 to Dana-Farber directly from your IRA without paying income taxes on the transfer. Plus, if you are 73 or older, your gift may satisfy your required minimum distribution and lower your taxable income. No matter your age, you can designate Dana-Farber and the Jimmy Fund as the beneficiary of all or a percentage of your IRA and it will pass to us tax-free after your lifetime.

Donor-Advised Fund (DAF)

Now is a great time to distribute a donation to Dana-Farber and the Jimmy Fund from your DAF. Recommend a grant from your DAF by December 31 to fuel groundbreaking discoveries and initiatives into the new year. You can name Dana-Farber as a beneficiary of your donor-advised fund as well!

Review and update account beneficiaries

The end of the year is a great time to review beneficiary designations on your bank, investment, and retirement accounts. Of course, loved ones are the first people to consider. After that, providing for causes you care about like Dana-Farber is an excellent way to demonstrate your values and make an impact on future generations.

jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Thanks to the tenacity and generosity of our entire community over the last seven years of The Dana-Farber Campaign, we are defying cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: National Cancer Center
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Five Dana-Farber investigators were recently awarded more than $250,000 from the National Cancer Center (NCC), whose mission is to provide financial support to researchers undertaking innovative and promising studies that seek to cure cancer. Since its founding 70 years ago, NCC has granted nearly $8 million in cancer research funding.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Day at Fenway
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Jimmy Fund Day at Fenway presented by DraftKings raised $230,000 to support innovative cancer research and compassionate patient care at Dana-Farber. Thanks to donor support, Dana-Farber patients and their families were able to participate in this unforgettable experience and take the field at Fenway Park.

img.alt_text: Jimmy Fund Day at Fenway logo

jetpack-related-posts.title: A new chapter in Dana-Farber leadership
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On October 1, 2024, Laurie H. Glimcher, MD, was succeeded by Benjamin L. Ebert, MD, PhD, as President and CEO of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute.

content.rendered:
Winter 2024
By Saul Wisnia

Jimmy Fund Vice President Suzanne Fountain retired in August after nearly 37 years overseeing grassroots fundraising for Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. During her storied career, Fountain has represented the Jimmy Fund at thousands of community events, mentored dozens of fundraising professionals, developed multi-generational relationships with families and supporters, and raised the bar of fundraising under the banner of the Jimmy Fund. Under her leadership, the Jimmy Fund has grown from a small number of events that generated about $1 million annually to a world-class, community fundraising pipeline for the Institute.

When she was hired by then-Jimmy Fund Chairman Mike Andrews in 1987, his staff numbered five. Fountain began traveling across New England to design and help run events, and Andrews quickly found her indispensable.

“Without question, Suzanne was the greatest hire I ever made,” Andrews reflects. “We created so many events that are still going on today, and we grew with them. Suzanne was and is a star.”

Indeed, many of today’s hallmark grassroots events were launched during Fountain’s tenure, from the Boston Marathon® Jimmy Fund Walk and Dana-Farber Marathon Challenge to the WEEI/NESN Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon. Others that were already established, like the Jimmy Fund Scooper Bowl®, Jimmy Fund Golf, and Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC), have reached new heights. Her dedication to Dana-Farber and the Jimmy Fund was recognized on a larger scale in 2022 when she received the Lifetime Achievement in Fundraising Award from the Association of Fundraising Professionals Massachusetts Chapter.

When not developing events, Fountain has often participated in them—including riding in the PMC, running the Falmouth Road Race, and driving a cart at Jimmy Fund Golf tournaments. And while she may be officially off the clock, she will continue to be involved as a volunteer and participant.

“There is a profound sense of pride and accomplishment for staff and volunteers who take part,” said Fountain, on what makes grassroots fundraising so special. “It’s an opportunity to give back and thank the place where they work or where they or their loved ones received the best care possible. Even if we can’t make someone better ourselves, grassroots fundraising is something we can do to support loved ones, cancer care, and research.”

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Golf supporter receives special award
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Longtime program sponsor and tournament organizer Michael Aizenstadt received Jimmy Fund Golf’s 2023 Ken Coleman Extra Mile Award from Suzanne Fountain, vice president of the Jimmy Fund, in recognition of over 35 years of dedication to the golf program.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Golf community helps to usher in the Jimmy Fund’s 75th
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Jimmy Fund Golf presented by Mohegan Sun marked another ace year in 2023, with an array of dedicated tournament directors, sponsors, and supporters across the country raising more than $6.8 million for The Dana-Farber Campaign.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Meet the new Co-Chairs of the Jimmy Fund: Brock Holt and Tom Caron
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Holt and Caron will be the lead ambassadors and public spokespeople on behalf of the Jimmy Fund, helping to raise funds and awareness.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Another home run year for the Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The WEEI/NESN Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon presented by Arbella Insurance helped strike out cancer for the 22nd year at Fenway Park in August, raising nearly $4 million for adult and pediatric cancer care and research at Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Little League
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Jimmy Fund Little League presented by the Yawkey Foundation surpassed its $275,000 goal, contributing $359,476 of unrestricted funding to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and underscoring the Yawkey Foundation’s dedication to advancing care for its community. The top fundraising team was North Reading 10U Gold, raising $18,465, and the top individual fundraiser, James Keohan, raised $10,617.

img.alt_text: Jimmy Fund Little League presented by Yawkey Foundation

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon breaks records with $5.7 million raised for Dana-Farber
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The WEEI/NESN Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon presented by Arbella Insurance continued to be a beacon of support for Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund in August with a record-breaking fundraising year.

img.alt_text: Ali Kelleher cheering at Fenway Park

content.rendered:
Winter 2024
By Lucy McDonald
Photography by Sam Ogden

AstraZeneca awarded over $360,000 to Dana-Farber to appoint a patient navigator to expand equitable access to clinical trials within the Breast Oncology Research Program. This navigator will proactively engage with patients with breast cancer and will focus on outreach and education to patients from historically marginalized communities to help navigate clinical trial complexities, logistics, and resources.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Expanding equitable access to critical care
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Last year, the National Breast Cancer Foundation (NBCF) generously provided $155,000 to support Dana-Farber’s inclusion, diversity, and equity work to ensure equitable health outcomes for all.

img.alt_text: National Breast Cancer Foundation, Inc. Logo

jetpack-related-posts.title: Khannas’ generous gift helps breast cancer patients navigate care
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Homai Khanna and her family are improving access to Dana-Farber's high-quality care with generous support for the Patient Navigator Program.

img.alt_text: A person wearing a mask and pointing to words on a sign

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign: Closing the equity gap in cancer care
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Funds from The Dana-Farber Campaign allow us to expand access to underserved populations and improve research to reduce disparities in treatment outcomes.

img.alt_text: Patient Navigator Judy Thyme, MSPH (left), assists patient Carle Price with her medications.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Expanding patient navigation through philanthropy
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With donor support through The Dana-Farber Campaign, the Institute piloted a new community-facing patient navigation program in 2021 to assist patients with transportation, language services, insurance, nutrition, and other social and economic concerns that may be barriers to care.

img.alt_text: Patient Navigator Marlene Escobar and Vice President of Community Health Magnolia Contreras are pictured outside of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Legacy of Leadership and Hope: The Elaine and Eduardo Saverin Foundation’s generational commitment to patients with metastatic breast cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Elaine and Eduardo Saverin Foundation has made an extraordinary $20 million grant to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute to accelerate research and care for people living with stage IV breast cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: American Cancer Society grants propel research and programs forward
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Cancer Society (ACS) recently awarded more than $3.1 million in grants to 11 Dana-Farber Cancer Institute investigators. These grants support various areas across Dana-Farber, including research on improved outcomes and patient assistance programming to help with access to care.

content.rendered:
Winter 2024
By Brendan Monahan

The Breast Cancer Alliance awarded a 2024 Young Investigator Grant of $125,000 to Sarah Naomi Olsen, PhD, accelerating her research on chromatin complexes in estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer. This impactful award will deepen our understanding of these unique complexes, laying the groundwork for new treatments which could significantly improve patient care.

jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Terri Brodeur Breast Cancer Foundation awarded $125,000 to Genevra Kuziel, PhD, supporting her research on estrogen receptor-positive (ER+) breast cancer, the most common breast cancer subtype with a high recurrence rate. Kuziel’s work aims to develop innovative combination therapies, with the goal of transforming treatment options and improving outcomes…

One explores circulating tumor DNA at critical timepoints in early stage hormone receptor-positive breast cancer, and the second assesses how chemotherapy effects the tumor-immune microenvironment and estrogen receptor activity in young…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Breast Cancer Alliance
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Breast Cancer Alliance awarded $125,000 to Dana-Farber to support research into the features of the tumor microenvironment that result in metastatic triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). This work will improve researchers’ knowledge of the behavior of TNBC and may help identify patients who are more likely to benefit from treatments such…

jetpack-related-posts.title: METAvivor advances metastatic breast cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: METAvivor, a non-profit organization that funds important research for stage IV metastatic breast cancer (MBC), has awarded research grants totaling $700,000 to three Dana-Farber faculty members

jetpack-related-posts.title: Susan G. Komen funds research into new breast cancer treatments
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In its mission to eradicate breast cancer, Susan G. Komen has invested nearly $1.1 billion in research since its founding in 1982. In 2023, Komen continued a longstanding partnership with Dana-Farber by awarding $2.3 million in new grants to Dana-Farber faculty members.

Winter 2024
By Lucy McDonald

The Cancer Nutrition Consortium awarded $110,000 to Dana-Farber to develop and test personalized nutrition plans for patients with cancer, aiming to improve their quality of life. This study will build on the guidelines previously established by the Cancer Nutrition Consortium.

jetpack-related-posts.title: National Foundation for Cancer Research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber recently received a $110,000 grant from the National Foundation for Cancer Research to study new, non-invasive approaches to identify specific subtypes of kidney cancer and particular genetic alterations in prostate cancer, with the aim of creating earlier detection and treatment interventions for patients with these diseases.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The success of our mission hinges on unrestricted gifts, including those raised through the Defy Cancer Fund.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign: Closing the equity gap in cancer care
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Funds from The Dana-Farber Campaign allow us to expand access to underserved populations and improve research to reduce disparities in treatment outcomes.

img.alt_text: Patient Navigator Judy Thyme, MSPH (left), assists patient Carle Price with her medications.

jetpack-related-posts.title: American Cancer Society grants propel research and programs forward
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Cancer Society (ACS) recently awarded more than $3.1 million in grants to 11 Dana-Farber Cancer Institute investigators. These grants support various areas across Dana-Farber, including research on improved outcomes and patient assistance programming to help with access to care.

jetpack-related-posts.title: William and Barbara Connolly
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s Sara M. Tolaney, MD, MPH, received a $100,000 gift from the Connolly Family Fund, established by William and Barbara Connolly, to advance innovative breast cancer research. Their support empowers Tolaney’s team to develop novel strategies for early detection, prevention, and personalized treatment, helping to improve outcomes for…

jetpack-related-posts.title: International Cancer Advocacy Network
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Exon 20 Group's International Research Consortium at the International Cancer Advocacy Network (ICAN) awarded $100,000 to Michael Eck, MD, PhD, to improve our understanding of common EGFR exon 20 insertion variants, which will be valuable for the development of potent and selective inhibitors for EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer.…

content.rendered:
Winter 2024
By Kayla Carcone
Photography by Jessamyn Martin

The For Kids’ Sake Foundation has generously donated $200,000 to establish the Malia’s Legacy Loves On Fellowship at Dana-Farber, in honor of Malia Jusczyk. This two-year fellowship, managed by Robbie Majzner, MD, will support neuroblastoma research focusing on enhancing GD2-targeted therapies and overcoming treatment resistance.
